fs_hz: not reported (beats resampled to 256 samples; source 360/250 Hz, listed as 350/240 in paper)
signal_length_s: 0.9 (0.4 s before to 0.5 s after R peak, resampled to 256 points)
loss_functions: Wasserstein GAN loss (critic without stated Lipschitz constraint); compared against JS/KL-based losses via loss curves
eval_metrics: PCC, PRD, RMSE per class vs DCGAN, QPatch-GAN, QCGAN-ECG, BiGRU-CNN GAN, BiLSTM-CNN GAN; classification accuracy of synthetic beats by Inception V3 pretrained on real beats (per class); generator/discriminator loss curves (convergence); robustness to simulated quantum noise channels (bit-flip, phase-flip, amplitude damping, depolarizing); visual inspection
notes: QRFGAN PCC only 0.05-0.61 per class (e.g. N 0.219 vs best baseline 0.174), PRD 0.75-1.08, RMSE 0.15-0.72; synthetic beats classified at 82.6% by real-trained Inception V3 vs 85.2% real baseline (QCGAN-ECG 79.8%, BiGRU-CNN 78.1%). Pairing protocol for PCC/PRD/RMSE on unconditional samples is undefined and the very low PCC suggests unpaired comparison; the utility section is described inconsistently as both train-on-synthetic and real-trained classifier applied to synthetic data (TRTS); no distribution/diversity metrics; 'no privacy risk' asserted without testing.

title: ECG-WM: A Physiology-Informed ECG World Model for Clinical Intervention Simulation
authors: Zhikang Chen; Yue Wang; Sen Cui; Yu Zhang; Changshui Zhang; Tianling Ren; Tingting Zhu
model_family: Hybrid (latent DDPM world model over frozen pretrained ECG VAE, with cardiac-ODE physiological energy regularization; VLM proposes interventions)
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG + MIMIC-IV-Clinical (17,493 patients, 108,980 patient-drug episodes); drug-response ECG datasets (ECGRDVQ and related FDA studies; 43 subjects, 8 regimens); in-house MIMIC-IV verapamil OOD set
loss_functions: VAE: reconstruction + KL (pretrained, frozen); diffusion: epsilon-prediction MSE + lambda_EPK (0.1) * latent energy ||z0_hat - Pi(e_EPK)||^2 to ODE-derived physiological anchor
eval_metrics: latent and signal MSE/MAE/RMSE (single and multi-step rollouts, rollout-oracle error); interval-normality Accuracy/Recall for QTc (Bazett), PR, Tpeak-Tend; OOD latent/signal error; Delta-risk Pearson, Spearman, sign agreement of ECG-FM diagnostic-score change; sample dispersion under prior perturbation
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: frozen ECG-FM foundation model (McKeen et al. 2025) producing 17 label probabilities as risk proxy
notes: States MSE insufficient; uses clinical interval-category agreement (QTc<=450/470 ms, PR 120-200 ms, Tpeak-Tend 80-113 ms; correct only if all labels match). Diagnostic-change agreement via frozen foundation model: Pearson 0.620 vs DADM 0.266. Compares WGAN, StyleGAN, ODE-GAN, TTS-CGAN, CECG-GAN, Diffusets, SE-Diff, DADM.

title: ECGrecover: a Deep Learning Approach for Electrocardiogram Signal Completion
authors: Alex Lence; Federica Granese; Ahmad Fall; Blaise Hanczar; Joe-Elie Salem; Jean-Daniel Zucker; Edi Prifti
model_family: Other (U-Net regression; compared with GAN baselines EKGAN, Pix2Pix, and CopyPaste)
task: lead-reconstruction + imputation (missing segments within a lead; full leads from a single lead)
datasets: Generepol (15,119 ECGs, 989 healthy subjects, before/after Sotalol); PTB-XL; LUDB
loss_functions: Composite L = MSE + alpha * Pearson-correlation loss (1 - r); alpha ablated in {0, 0.1, 0.5, 1, inf}
eval_metrics: RMSE; maximum absolute error (MAE); DTW; Pearson correlation coefficient (PCC); delta-QT distance (neurokit2 Q and T peak detection per beat); SQI Avg-QRS and SQI Fuzzy (% unacceptable); downstream TdP-risk DenseNet accuracy with augmentation (5 seeds); statistical tests (p<2e-16)
notes: Delta-QT shows CopyPaste trivially preserves QT, a metric pitfall. Hybrid MSE+Pearson loss balances amplitude and synchrony; Pearson-only gives high PCC but poor other metrics. Expert cardiologists curated data. Augmentation raised TdP accuracy 92.47 -> 93.84%.

title: ECGTwin: Personalized ECG Generation Using Controllable Diffusion Model
authors: Yongfan Lai; Bo Liu; Xinyan Guan; Qinghao Zhao; Hongyan Li; Shenda Hong
model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM, DiT or U-Net backbone, AdaX condition injector; contrastive Individual Base Extractor)
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (+ MIMIC-IV-Clinical); PTB-XL (external)
loss_functions: Stage 1: symmetric CLIP-style InfoNCE contrastive loss (cosine similarity, learnable τ) on same-patient ECG pairs; Stage 2: DDPM noise-prediction MSE; pre-trained VAE decoder
eval_metrics: FID; improved precision/recall/F1 (Kynkäänniemi); HR-MAE; CLIP score; intra-/inter-individual similarity score (cosine); silhouette coefficient; t-SNE; downstream personalized normal/abnormal classification accuracy and macro-F1 (patient-wise and population-wise)
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: same as DiffuSETS three-level protocol (pretrained ECG encoder; not restated)
notes: Reuses DiffuSETS three-level evaluation; adds identity-preservation metrics (similarity score = mean intra-patient minus inter-patient cosine; silhouette). Baselines LAVQ, DiffuSETS-p. CLIP lower on PTB-XL due to German reports.

title: Electrocardiogram Synthesis from Photoplethysmogram Signals Through Generative Adversarial Networks
authors: Victor Ramon França Bezerra de Souza; Lucas Bernardino Cardoso; Ângelo Perkusich; Gutemberg Gonçalves dos Santos Júnior
venue: IEEE Latin American Symposium on Circuits and Systems (LASCAS)
model_family: GAN (CardioGAN-style: Attention U-Net generator, dual time-domain and FFT frequency-domain discriminators)
datasets: BIDMC; CapnoBase (CAPNO); PPG-DaLiA; WESAD; custom synchronized PPG–ECG recordings (MAX30100 finger PPG + AD8232 3-electrode lead II, Arduino at 480 Hz)
fs_hz: 128 (resampled; text also states 120 Hz for custom data)
loss_functions: LSGAN adversarial (time + frequency discriminators) + L1
eval_metrics: MSE (z-scored signals); Pearson correlation; 'similarity' = (1−MSE)x100%; SNR improvement of notch filter; qualitative time/frequency plots; comparison vs CardioGAN (Sarkar) and Belhasin diffusion (reported numbers)
notes: MSE 0.278±0.05, ρ 0.68±0.03, similarity 72.2% (unfiltered MSE 0.384, ρ 0.52); worse than Belhasin 2024 (MSE 0.222, ρ 0.71), better than Sarkar (0.364, 0.63), but baselines are copied numbers with different preprocessing and splits (authors admit). No subject-split details, no clinical/HR metrics, number of custom subjects not reported; notch filter gives ~20 dB SNR gain.

title: End-to-end non-invasive ECG signal generation from PPG signal: a self-supervised learning approach
authors: Murat Yalcin; Marc Erich Latoschik
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP with Transformer-based generator/discriminator; self-supervised pretraining of discriminator via signal-transformation recognition)
datasets: Who is Alyx? (VR dataset, ECG 130 Hz / Empatica PPG 64 Hz); MIMIC III matched waveform (125 Hz); MIMIC PERform AF (AF detection); pretraining: BIDMC, CapnoBase, WESAD
signal_length_s: windows of 4-160 s (best 64 s Who is Alyx?, 96 s MIMIC III); 30 s for AF task
loss_functions: WGAN-GP adversarial (Wasserstein + gradient penalty, lambda tuned); self-supervised pretext loss: six-way signal-transformation recognition (noise, scaling, temporal inversion, permutation, negation, time-warping)
eval_metrics: Frechet Distance (discrete curve FD); RMSE (mV); Pearson correlation; MAE of heart rate (MAEHR, generated ECG vs PPG); MMD^2 and squared Energy Distance with permutation-test p-values on embeddings; t-SNE; AF detection accuracy/precision/recall/F1 with varying synthetic proportions
notes: LOSO evaluation. Best RMSE 0.168 mV, rho 0.952 (MIMIC III, 96 s). HR error reduced 83.9%/72.4% vs PPG. 'FD' here is discrete Frechet curve distance, not FID-style. MMD^2 0.011 (p=0.84). Pitfall: using own discriminator as embedding extractor for MMD/ED is biased.

title: Enhancing cardiac disease recognition with generative model-based data augmentation
authors: Oscal Tzyh-Chiang Chen; Yue-Han Li; Chuan-Wen Wang; Guo-Zua Wu
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, 200 steps; DeScoD-ECG-based backbone with enhanced half-normalized filters, modified ELAN, multi-scale convs 3/5/9/15, time-adaptive weighting; CLIP text-encoder conditioning)
task: text-conditional (disease-description prompt) class augmentation of hypertrophy
datasets: PTB-XL (5 superclasses; 8:1:1 split; HYP augmented with 1,000 or 2,000 synthetic ECGs)
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, II, V1-V6; remaining 4 computed)
loss_functions: not reported explicitly (standard DDPM denoising objective implied)
eval_metrics: per-class and mean AUC of InceptionTime multi-label classifier trained with vs without synthetic augmentation; ablations on blocks/ELAN placement; comparison against published PTB-XL classifiers
notes: Augmenting HYP with 2,000 synthetic ECGs raises InceptionTime mean AUC 92.45 -> 93.20% (Type-3, 5 blocks; HYP 90.29 -> 90.84, MI 91.68 -> 93.77) vs DeScoD-based baseline 92.84%. Utility-only evaluation: no fidelity, distribution or clinical-plausibility metrics, single run with no variance, and gains (<1% AUC) are within typical seed noise.

title: Enhancing Inter-Lead Correlations: A Novel Diffusion GAN Framework for 12-Lead ECG Generation
authors: Yongchao Wang; Fubin Guo; Shizhan Tang; Junchao Fan; Xiuli Bi; Bin Xiao
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics, Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP 2026)
model_family: Hybrid Diffusion-GAN (EDIFFGAN: denoising-diffusion GAN, conditional generator outputs 9 electrode potentials, electrode superposition module derives 12 leads; frozen ResNet34 classifier guidance)
task: class-cond 12-lead heartbeat generation (PTB-XL superclasses STTC, MI, NORM, CD, HYP) for augmentation
datasets: PTB-XL (500 Hz, 21,837 records, 5 diagnostic superclasses)
loss_functions: Denoising-diffusion-GAN adversarial loss on (x_t, x_{t-1}) pairs (WGAN-style critic) + cross-entropy classification loss from frozen pretrained ResNet34
eval_metrics: ECGLS (proposed: sum of DTW distances between limb leads and their Einthoven/Goldberger derivations); FID; generation time for 20,000 samples; augmentation (1:1 real+synthetic) ResNet34 AUROC/precision/recall/F1 on PTB-XL; ECGLS sensitivity test under Gaussian noise and point omission; visual comparison
notes: EDIFFGAN ECGLS 1.32e-5 vs 4.85-155.44 for CGAN/CWGAN/TCGAN/DDPM-2D; FID 2.12 (CGAN 5.14, DDPM-2D 7.18); 2.63 s per 20k samples vs 2606.78 s DDPM-2D; augmentation F1 0.7171 vs baseline 0.6174 (AUROC 0.9431 vs 0.9046). ECGLS is near zero by construction for any model that derives limb leads from electrodes (ESM), so the comparison is partly tautological; it only checks limb-lead consistency (not precordial), and the FID embedding network is not specified.

title: Evaluating the feasibility of 12-lead electrocardiogram reconstruction from limited leads using deep learning
authors: Oriana Presacan; Alexandru Dorobanțiu; Jonas Lynggaard Isaksen; Tobias Willi; Claus Graff; Michael Alexander Riegler; Arun Raghav Mahankali Sridhar; Jørgen Kim Kanters; Vajira Lasantha Thambawita
model_family: GAN (Pulse2Pulse/pix2pix-inspired U-Net generator, WGAN-GP) and U-Net (MSE) baseline
datasets: PTB-XL v1.0.3 (9514 individuals; test 952 normal ECGs)
loss_functions: GAN: WGAN-GP adversarial (with gradient clipping) + L1 reconstruction; U-Net: MSE
eval_metrics: Per-lead RMSE; GE MUSE 12SL measurements (RR, QT, PR, QRS duration, R/S/T peak, ST amplitudes); Student t-test (means); F-test (variances); Bland-Altman plots; R2/Pearson between error and true amplitude (regression-to-mean); inter-lead marker correlations real vs reconstructed
notes: Key metric criticism: low RMSE hides regression-to-the-mean. Reconstructed amplitudes have reduced variance (F-test p<0.05); error vs true amplitude R2=0.92 (V3); inter-lead R-amplitude R2 I-V3 0.04 real vs 0.49 reconstructed. Concludes not clinically usable.

title: Evaluating the Quality of CycleGAN Generated ECG Data for Myocardial Infarction Classification
authors: Sara Battiston; Roberto Sassi; Massimo Walter Rivolta
model_family: GAN (CycleGAN style transfer, 2 CycleGANs / 4 generators)
datasets: PTB-XL (10,776 ECGs: NORM, ASMI, IMI)
loss_functions: CycleGAN losses (adversarial + cycle consistency, as in Zhu et al.; not detailed)
eval_metrics: 95% confidence-band plots per lead; UMAP 2D density/scatter (fit on real); GAN-train score; GAN-test score (vs baselines); ST-segment amplitude comparison via modified Hotelling T² simultaneous 95% intervals per lead
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (UMAP on raw signals); CNN classifier (ResNet-style, reduced) for GAN-train/test
notes: Negative result: GAN-train 62% vs baseline 98%; GAN-test 81% vs baseline 89%; ST amplitudes significantly different in all conditions; distributions overlapped only in tails. Warns image-domain GANs cannot simply be adapted to ECG.

title: Exploring latent diffusion models for ECG generation on the minute scale
authors: Dominik D. Kranz; Jan F. Kraemer; Oruç Kahriman; Alexander Nelde; Niels Wessel; Christian Meisel
venue: Computer Methods and Programs in Biomedicine
model_family: Diffusion (latent: VQ-VAE with 1024-token codebook on 5 s windows + 1D U-Net DDIM backbone with bottleneck self-attention; ECGEN)
task: class-cond (sinus vs AFib, 30 s); inpainting/outpainting (90 s); unconditional long-duration (320 s)
datasets: Private: single-lead stroke-unit ECGs, Charité Berlin (440k 30 s, 220k 90 s, 200k 320 s segments; AFib/sinus labelled by Zhou symbolic-entropy detector)
loss_functions: VQ-VAE MSE reconstruction (pretrained separately) + standard DDIM/DDPM noise-prediction L2 loss
eval_metrics: Conditioning accuracy via Zhou entropy AFib detector (AUC); HR and SDNN distributions vs training set (two-sample KS test, permutation test of means); inpainting HR consistency (left/inpainted/right segments, KS, permutation); inpainting coherence (256 inpaintings of same ECG); averaged-beat RMSE, MAE, DTW, Fréchet distance; averaged-beat intervals (PR, QRS, QT, ST, Tpeak-Tend); 8 ms gap inpainting RMSE/MAE/DTW/FD vs interpolation; expert inspection of morphological implausibility rate
notes: Small: AFib-vs-sinus AUC 0.98 but ~12% of sinus prompts classified AFib; HR 71.38 vs 70.57 bpm, SDNN 75.79 vs 151.02 (KS p<0.001). Large: HR 72.66±12.22 vs 70.82±3.40 and SDNN 89.06 vs 398.33 (distributions narrower and shifted), ~1.5% of beats implausible (double R peaks) by expert review. Inpainting halves RMSE/MAE/DTW/FD vs interpolation; morphology metrics are computed on grand-average beats, which hides beat-level variability; private data.

title: Exploring multimodal generative approaches in cardiovascular disease: A five-year systematic literature review
authors: Xinyu Tian; Sio Kei Im; Kefeng Li; Wei Ke
model_family: Survey/EvalOnly (PRISMA systematic review of GAN, VAE, Transformer/LLM-VLM and diffusion methods for multimodal CVD data)
datasets: review of 46 empirical studies 2021-2025 (11 core multimodal-generative, 16 single-modality generative, 12 multimodal non-generative, 7 interpretation/reporting) + 39 background sources; modalities MRI, CT, PET, ECG, PPG, PCG, EHR/tabular, clinical text
loss_functions: not applicable
eval_metrics: Reviewed: PSNR, SSIM, Dice, Hausdorff (image synthesis/segmentation); accuracy, AUC, F1, precision, recall (prediction); SNR, MSE, RMSE, PRD, FD, MAE, DTW and downstream arrhythmia accuracy (signal generation); FID/FVD; KS and TVD for synthetic EHR; radiologist reader studies; custom 5-item PROBAST/QUADAS-2-inspired quality checklist
notes: PRISMA review of 9 databases (701 records, 531 screened, 46 included); GANs used in 16/46 studies, Transformers/LLMs 11, VAEs 4, diffusion only 1. ECG-generation content is thin (CardioGAN, MC-WGAN of Cretu et al., quantum cGAN, cGAN denoising, PPG->ECG of Ding et al.); signal generation is judged 'proof-of-concept' evaluated mainly by SNR/MSE and downstream accuracy, with pathological-feature retention and diagnostic equivalence untested; no study had prospective clinical validation and heterogeneous metrics precluded meta-analysis, so the authors call for standardised benchmarks and evaluation protocols.

title: f-GAN: A frequency-domain-constrained generative adversarial network for PPG to ECG synthesis
authors: Nathan C. L. Kong; Dae Lee; Huyen Do; Dae Hoon Park; Cong Xu; Hongda Mao; Jonathan Chung
model_family: GAN (f-GAN: U-Net-style encoder-decoder generator, standard adversarial loss + frequency-domain constraint)
datasets: PPG-DaLiA (15 participants, subject-disjoint 9/3/3 split)
loss_functions: Original GAN minimax adversarial loss + lambda_freq (0.1) * L1 distance between FFT amplitude spectra (excluding DC) of generated and real ECG
eval_metrics: Heart-rate MAPE (peak detector on synthetic vs real ECG); number of heart-rate estimation failure cases (peak detector fails); comparison with PPG peak-detection HR baseline; qualitative waveform inspection
notes: Argues HR error is more interpretable than RMSE. Novel 'pipeline-compatibility' metric: count of segments where standard peak detection fails on synthetic ECG. 31 random seeds with t-tests (p=0.005). Frequency constraint lowers HR error ~2% and variance.

title: FlowECG: Using Flow Matching to Create a More Efficient ECG Signal Generator
authors: Vitalii Bondar; Serhii Semenov; Vira Babenko; Dmytro Holovniak
model_family: FlowMatching (rectified/linear-path flow matching on SSSD-ECG S4 backbone)
datasets: PTB-XL
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 derived)
loss_functions: Flow matching L2 velocity regression ||f(x_t,c,t)-(x1-x0)||^2 (baseline SSSD-ECG: diffusion MSE noise prediction)
eval_metrics: DTW; 1-Wasserstein distance on handcrafted statistical/temporal/spectral features; MMD; spectral similarity score 1/(1+mean W(PSD_real,PSD_gen)); NFE vs quality curves; all per-lead averaged
notes: At 200 NFE: MMD 21.09 vs 80.70 (SSSD-ECG), DTW 83.96 vs 73.49, W 0.62 vs 1.03, SimScore 0.37 vs 0.30. Comparable quality at 10-25 NFE. Explicitly notes field lacks standardized protocols. No utility or clinical metrics.

title: Generating High-Fidelity Synthetic ECG Signals Using Deep Autoencoder Architectures
authors: Anisha Riya; Abdullah Bin Queyam
venue: Artificial Intelligence and Smart Technologies for Sustainability Conference (AISTS)
model_family: VAE / Autoencoders (LSTM-AE, 1D CNN-AE, VAE, denoising AE compared)
task: reconstruction (autoencoding of real ECG presented as synthesis)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia Database (examples from record 101)
loss_functions: MSE reconstruction; VAE adds KL divergence; DAE reconstructs clean from corrupted input
eval_metrics: final training MSE loss; Pearson correlation with original; SNR (dB); training time; RR-interval agreement (Pearson r, mean RR, MAE, RMSE) for CNN-AE; qualitative waveform overlays
notes: CNN-AE: loss 5e-6, PCC 0.999966, SNR 51.18 dB (LSTM-AE 0.999866 / 44.62 dB; VAE 0.9935 / 28.56 dB; DAE 0.9852 / 24.10 dB); RR intervals r = 1.000, mean RR 0.845 s identical, RMSE 1 ms. All metrics are paired reconstruction of input signals (largely training data under K-fold), so no new samples are generated or tested for distribution match, diversity, privacy or utility; the 'state-of-the-art synthetic ECG' claim is unsupported.

title: Generating Precordial-lead Electrocardiogram from Smartwatch
authors: Hyeon-Hwa Choi; Segyeong Joo
model_family: GAN (pix2pix-style U-Net generator, 5-layer conv discriminator; one model per precordial lead)
datasets: Asan Medical Center 12-lead records (training); 10 healthy volunteers, Galaxy Watch4 + standard 12-lead (100 test recordings)
loss_functions: not reported
eval_metrics: Fréchet distance (FD, per lead); MSE (per lead)
notes: Mean FD 15.46, MSE 0.0937; V1 best (FD 4.69), V3/V4 worst (~21). FD formula given as Gaussian Fréchet (mean+covariance), described as curve similarity — ambiguous. Very small real-world test set.

title: Generating Realistic Multi-Beat ECG Signals
authors: Paul Pöhl; Viktor Schlegel; Hao Li; Anil Bharath
model_family: Hybrid (beat-level time-series Diffusion with prompt bases + multivariate feature-sequence generator + feature-guided beat matching/stitching)
datasets: MIT-BIH Supraventricular Arrhythmia Database (main); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (additional test)
signal_length_s: single beats ~100-200 samples; long-form sequences (e.g., 100 beats)
loss_functions: not reported
eval_metrics: Beat level: DTW, Frechet distance, Euclidean distance, RMSE, MAE, MSE, PRD between average beats; average KL, JS divergence, MMD, Wasserstein, KS statistic, mean/variance/skewness differences. Features: per-feature KL, MMD, Wasserstein, KS, mean difference; feature correlation matrices; density-difference heatmap. Utility: TSTR accuracy/precision/recall/F1 (SVM, Balanced SVM, Decision Tree, Naive Bayes, and others); R-amplitude matching rate
notes: Long-form ECGs outperform end-to-end long diffusion in TSTR. Pitfall: many fidelity metrics computed only between AVERAGE beats (e.g., DTW 2.07, PRD 8.53), which hides diversity/mode collapse. Inter-feature correlation preservation (RR, P/Q/T intervals) is a useful multi-beat check.

title: Generating Time Series Data With Real-Valued DC-GAN From Complex Time-Frequency Domain: Application to ECG Synthesis
authors: Bertan Karahoda
model_family: GAN (2-D real-valued DC-GAN: 3 transposed-conv generator, 5-conv discriminator, batch size 1; real/imag STFT coefficients embedded in RGB channels of 78x78 images; inverse STFT to waveform)
task: class-wise synthesis (one GAN per class: N, V, F beats; 5 s AF and VT rhythm strips)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII beats); MIT-BIH Atrial Fibrillation; MIT-BIH Malignant Ventricular Ectopy (VT)
signal_length_s: 0.75 (beats: 350 ms before to 400 ms after R, 270 samples); 5 (AF/VT)
loss_functions: standard DC-GAN adversarial loss
eval_metrics: MSE; RMSE; DTW between selected generated samples and visually matched original samples; visual inspection of time-frequency coefficients and waveforms
notes: Beat MSE on the order of 1e-7 (better than Neifar et al.); AF RMSE 6.86e-4, MSE 4.70e-7, DTW 24.3; VT RMSE 7.80e-4, MSE 6.08e-7, DTW 59.6. Metrics are computed only on a handful of generated samples each paired with an original beat chosen by visual similarity (cherry-picked, no distributional, diversity, utility or memorisation analysis), so extremely low errors may indicate copying rather than quality.

title: Generation and Selection: A Self-Iterative Two-Stage Data Augmentation Method for Automated ECG Classification
authors: Chaoying Jiang; Yujing Xin; Ning Liu; Yonghui Xu; Lei Liu; Lizhen Cui; Jianyong Wang
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
model_family: Diffusion (unconditional DDPM with Transformer-encoder noise predictor, 6 layers, 1000 steps) + classifier-confidence pseudo-label selection with self-iterative retraining (SiTs-ECG)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI 5-class beats); Apnea-ECG (1-min segments, apnea vs normal); PTB-XL (multi-label superclasses, 100 Hz)
loss_functions: standard DDPM epsilon-MSE; cross-entropy / BCE for downstream classifiers with pseudo-labels (threshold lambda=0.5)
eval_metrics: downstream Precision/Recall/F1/Accuracy (ResNet34, ECG-Transformer, 5 repeats); Context-FID; discriminative score |0.5-Acc|; predictive score (train-on-synthetic next-step MAE on real); PCA visualisation; paired t-test + Cohen's d; threshold ablation; low-data (1k/5k/10k) experiments; training/sampling time
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: Context-FID encoder (TS2Vec-style per PSA-GAN; not specified further)
notes: Apnea-ECG with ECG-Transformer: +0.079 P, +0.091 R, +0.092 F1, +0.073 Acc (paired t-test p 0.036-0.047, Cohen's d > 0.8); MIT-BIH ResNet34 R/F1/Acc 0.755/0.763/0.994; PTB-XL P/R/F1/Acc 0.816/0.797/0.801/0.878. Discriminative and predictive scores < 0.1 and near-best Context-FID vs ECG-Augmentation, AC-WGAN-GP, ECG-GAN (Context-FID 37.4 on MIT-BIH), SSSD-ECG; quality tables are images not in the text. Classifier-confidence filtering selects 'easy' samples and may reduce diversity; no clinical or privacy checks.

title: Generation of Realistic Synthetic ECG Data Using Uncertainty-Aware Diffusion Model
authors: Qi Zhang; Hongyan Li
venue: Computer Graphics International (CGI 2025), Lecture Notes in Computer Science vol. 16509
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM with uncertainty guidance: Dirichlet posterior network with class-conditional normalizing flows; gradient of log-concentration added to noise prediction)
task: class-cond 12-lead ECG generation (PTB-XL superclasses NORM, MI, STTC, CD, HYP)
datasets: PTB-XL (100 Hz, 10 s, 12-lead)
loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction L2 + λ·Bayesian posterior-network loss (expected cross-entropy under Dirichlet minus entropy regulariser)
eval_metrics: Blinded expert review by one cardiologist (real vs synthetic identification among 1 real + 3 synthetic per case, vs Pulse2Pulse and SSSD-ECG); qualitative per-class case study (real vs synthetic pairs); visual inspection
notes: No quantitative metrics at all: evaluation is a single cardiologist's blinded authenticity review with anecdotal examples (Pulse2Pulse flagged for absent P waves/irregular RR, SSSD for inconsistent P waves) and a qualitative per-class case study; number of cases and identification rates are not reported. Claims of outperforming SOTA are therefore unsupported numerically; authors acknowledge downstream-classifier utility gap.

title: Generative adversarial networks (GANs) to produce synthetic 12-lead electrocardiogram signals for specific and rare diseases: a novel, powerful tool towards clinical advancements
authors: Panteleimon Pantelidis; Evangelos K. Oikonomou; Maria Bampa; Ioannis Gialamas; Athina Goliopoulou; Vasiliki Chara Mystakidi; George-Angelo Papamikroulis; Μichael Spartalis; Dimitris Tsiachris; Theo Papaioannou; Kostas Kalogeras; Manolis Vavouranakis; Panagiotis Papapetrou; Gerasimos Siasos
venue: European Heart Journal (Suppl 1, ESC Congress abstract)
model_family: GAN (general-purpose GAN pre-trained on PTB-XL, feeding 'DeceptionECG', an InceptionTime-inspired disease-specific GAN)
task: class-cond (disease-specific: AF, anterior STEMI, WPW and other abnormalities; augmentation and medical education)
datasets: PTB-XL (>21,000 ECGs; disease annotations validated by two electrophysiologists)
loss_functions: not reported (adversarial GAN loss)
eval_metrics: independent DL discriminator real-vs-synthetic accuracy; cardiologist real-vs-synthetic accuracy (Turing test, 2 clinicians); InceptionTime-variant disease classifier trained on real, accuracy on synthetic normal vs target disease (TRTS); augmentation accuracy (1,589 real + 5,000 synthetic, tested on 1,000 real); generation speed
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (InceptionTime-variant classifiers for discrimination and disease recognition)
code_available: stated as available online (URL not given)
notes: Anterior STEMI: discriminator accuracy 48.9%, clinicians 56% and 51% (chance level); TRTS disease-recognition accuracy 88.7%; augmentation 94.6% vs 89.3% real-only; 2,500 12-lead ECGs/min. Source is a one-page conference abstract with no architecture, signal-format, sample-size-per-test or statistical detail; no distributional or privacy metrics despite the privacy motivation.

title: Generative Adversarial Networks for Modeling Bio-Electric Fields in Medicine: A Review of EEG, ECG, EMG, and EOG Applications
authors: Jiaqi Liang; Yuheng Zhou; Kai Ma; Yifan Jia; Yadan Zhang; Bangcheng Han; Min Xiang
model_family: Survey (GANs for EEG/ECG/EMG/EOG)
datasets: catalogued: MIT-BIH, PTB-XL and others across modalities
loss_functions: Catalogues GAN loss variants with formulas: WGAN (Wasserstein), WGAN-GP (gradient penalty), BGAN, EBGAN, LSGAN, conditional GAN/CWGAN; mentions physiological constraints in GAN losses and feature-loss functions for denoising
eval_metrics: Catalogued (synthesis): PRD; RMSE; FD; MAE; DTW; Fréchet/Euclidean distance; SSIM; FID; IS; sliced Wasserstein distance; MMD; Kappa; classification accuracy/F1/AUC; (denoising): SNR; RRMSE (time/frequency); CC; PSNR; MI; PRD
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: not reported (FID usage in catalogued works, extractor unspecified)
notes: Proposes task-specific evaluation framework; flags pitfalls: subject-wise data leakage inflating classifier-based quality proxies and 'metric-task mismatch' (fidelity judged only by statistical similarity rather than preservation of diagnostic features). Calls for standardized protocols and physiological constraints in losses.

title: Generative Data by β-Variational Autoencoders Help Build Stronger Classifiers: ECG Use Case
authors: Yousef Nademi; Sunil V. Kalmady; Weijie Sun; Amir Salimi; Abram Hindle; Padma Kaul; Russell Greiner
venue: International Symposium on Medical Information Processing and Analysis (SIPAIM)
model_family: VAE (beta-VAE, beta=8, 32-d latent; van de Leur et al. architecture adapted to 12-lead rhythm)
task: augmentation (posterior-sampled 12-lead STE ECGs from real STE inputs, added to CPSC 2018)
datasets: private Alberta (AB) 12-lead ECG dataset (244,077 patients, 15 ICD-10 diagnoses); CPSC 2018
loss_functions: beta-VAE objective (reconstruction + beta-weighted KL, beta=8)
eval_metrics: downstream InceptionTime multi-label per-label F1 on CPSC 2018 with 10,000-sample bootstrap 95% CIs and bootstrapped paired F1 differences; embedding quality via XGBoost AUROC/F1 on 15 diagnoses; correlation of latent embeddings with 22 Philips ECG global measurements
code_available: not reported (footnote says code available, link missing in PDF)
notes: Adding 1072 VAE-generated STE ECGs raised STE F1 by +0.046 [0.027-0.066] vs +0.089 for 1072 real AB STE ECGs and +0.045 for oversampling; improved 4 other labels but STD F1 dropped -0.13. Only utility evaluated - no waveform fidelity, diversity or clinical-feature metrics; synthetic ECGs are encoder-posterior samples of real STE ECGs (near-reconstructions), and privacy is asserted but not tested.

title: Generative Reconstruction of Multimodal Cardiac Waveforms From a Single Vibrational Cardiography Sensor
authors: James Skoric; Yannick D'Mello; David V. Plant
venue: IEEE Journal of Biomedical and Health Informatics
model_family: GAN (conditional, 1D pix2pix: U-Net generator, PatchGAN discriminator, no dropout)
task: other-modality→ECG translation (6-axis VCG/SCG+GCG → ECG, ICG, NIBP, PPG simultaneously)
datasets: Private McGill dataset: 20 healthy subjects (16 M/4 F), 34 sessions, 2,686 min, VCG at xiphoid + Biopac ECG/ICG/NIBP/PPG; rest, breath-hold, deep breathing, cold pressor; 118,772 windows
loss_functions: pix2pix: L1 reconstruction + binary cross-entropy adversarial loss (PatchGAN)
eval_metrics: Pearson correlation (per subject, median); MAE (per subject, median) on z-scored signals; per-intervention R/MAE; fiducial-point timing MAE and mean error (ECG P/Q/R/S/T peaks via NeuroKit2; ICG B/C/X; PPG onset/peak; NIBP systolic/diastolic); window-size sensitivity; correlation of error with demographics
notes: Leave-one-subject-out: median ECG R 0.808 (NIBP 0.907, ICG 0.833, PPG 0.929), ECG MAE 0.309 (z-scored); ECG R-peak timing MAE 6.66 ms, P/Q/S/T 12.25-28.47 ms; at 20.48 s windows ECG R 0.789. Paired evaluation on amplitude-normalised signals only (absolute amplitudes not recovered); fiducial matches >250 ms apart discarded as annotation failures, which can flatter timing errors; small healthy cohort.

title: Graph-Based ECG Synthesis with Activation-Consistency Certification and Diagnostics-Aware Morphology Curation
authors: Yongjun Yoo
model_family: Other (biophysical graph-based simulator: Eikonal-template ET and pseudo-diffusion reaction-Eikonal RE backends; not a deep generative model)
task: other (mechanistic synthetic ECG generation + curation; synthetic pretraining)
datasets: simulated 12-lead ECGs; PTB-XL+ (delineation fine-tuning/evaluation)
signal_length_s: single beats; 12 s concatenated traces for pretraining
loss_functions: none for generator (simulation); delineation segmentation model loss not reported
eval_metrics: Bellman residual certificate (activation-time consistency); R² of RE vs Eikonal activation times; activation-order diagnostics; P/QRS/T amplitudes, intervals, polarity checks, morphology-failure flags; recovery plausibility score; feature-space coverage (fraction of occupied feature bins); acceptance yield; P/QRS/T delineation IoU after synthetic pretraining on 1-10% PTB-XL+ labels
notes: Two-stage diagnostics (metric computation separated from acceptance policy). Acceptance 658/2000 RE vs 578/2000 ET; coverage 0.09888 vs 0.09248. Synthetic pretraining stabilised low-label delineation (T-wave IoU std ≤0.003 vs 0.247). Not a learned generator; relevant mostly for curation/validity filters.

title: High-Fidelity Synthetic ECG Generation via Mel-Spectrogram Informed Diffusion Training
authors: Zhuoyi Huang; Nutan Sahoo; Anamika Kumari; Girish Kumar; Kexuan Cai; Shixing Cao; Yue Kang; Tian Xia; Somya Chatterjee; Nicholas Hausman; Aidan Jay; Eric S. Rosenthal; Soundar Srinivasan; Sadid Hasan; Alex Fedorov; Sulaiman Vesal
model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG backbone, score-based diffusion with structured state-space layers; MIDT-ECG)
task: class-cond (diagnosis + demographic conditioning: age, gender, height, weight)
datasets: PTB-XL (standard patient-level splits)
loss_functions: MSE denoising loss + beta * L1 multi-resolution Mel-spectrogram loss (multi-window STFT, Mel-warped)
eval_metrics: RMSE; MSE; SNR; Fourier distance; Hausdorff distance; SSIM; Membership Inference Risk (MIR); Nearest-Neighbor Adversarial Accuracy (NNAA); inter-lead Pearson correlation matrix error; clinical feature distributions (e.g. QT); label faithfulness (real-trained classifier agreement); downstream AUROC in data substitution/augmentation (synthetic-only, mixed folds); outlier analysis (Q3+3IQR); visual Turing-style comparison
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: classifier trained on real PTB-XL for faithfulness/AUROC (architecture not detailed in extracted text)
notes: Proposes multi-pillar benchmark (fidelity, personalization, privacy, utility). Synthetic-only training AUROC 0.640 vs SSSD-ECG 0.541. Inter-lead correlation-matrix error is a key metric. Faithfulness used as both metric and filter. Gains 4-8% over baseline. Outlier lead-distribution analysis.

title: Hybrid Quantum-Classical Generative Adversarial Network for Synthetic 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Signal Generation
authors: Aron Jose A; A. Shamila Ebenezer
venue: International Conference on Recent Advancement in Electrical, Computer and Communication Technologies (IECCT)
model_family: GAN (hybrid quantum-classical: 4-qubit, 4-layer PennyLane PQC generator with angle encoding, ~1,024 params + 1D-CNN discriminator; parameter-shift gradients, simulated)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
n_leads: 12 (claimed; 'reconstructed' from the 2 MIT-BIH channels via Einthoven/Goldberger relations)
loss_functions: standard non-saturating GAN BCE losses; Adam lr 1e-4, 500 epochs
eval_metrics: Fréchet distance ('FID adapted for time series', feature space unspecified); SNR (dB); training stability/loss curves; qualitative P/QRS/T and inter-lead checks; latent traversal over 200 seeds; claimed amplitude/HRV/duration statistical similarity (no numbers); SVM PVC F1 with 30% synthetic replacement
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: not reported (FD computed on unspecified features)
notes: QGAN FD 12.3±2.1 vs classical CNN 15.8±3.2 and LSTM 18.4±4.1; SNR 28.6 vs 24.1/19.3 dB; +4.2% PVC F1 with augmentation. Many red flags: 12 leads cannot be derived from MIT-BIH's MLII + one precordial lead, 4-qubit measurements post-processed into 12x250 outputs is unexplained, FD feature space and SNR reference for unpaired samples are undefined, no seeds/CIs protocol, and clinical-interval/HRV similarity is asserted without numbers.

title: Implicit Neural Representations for ECG Synthesis: What is the Potential ?
authors: Nour Neifar; Achraf Ben Hamadou
venue: IEEE/ACS International Conference on Computer Systems and Applications (AICCSA)
model_family: Diffusion (class-conditional DDPM with Attention U-Net on 2D implicit representations: SDF / occupancy grids, wavelet coarse+detail predictor, and INR feature planes with shared MLP decoder; marching-squares signal extraction)
task: class-cond (representation study: implicit vs explicit ECG representations)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
signal_length_s: not reported (short beat-level segments rendered as 64x64 to 1024x1024 grids)
loss_functions: DDPM denoising loss; MSE for wavelet detail-coefficient predictor; joint reconstruction for INR encoder/MLP decoder (occupancy)
eval_metrics: qualitative visual inspection of generated grids/signals; GPU memory and time per epoch vs grid resolution; qualitative comparison with explicit-representation generators (GAN, anchored GAN, shape-prior GAN, DiffECG, SSSD-ECG)
notes: Negative/exploratory result: SDF diffusion did not converge, occupancy grids were noisy, and the INR feature-plane DDPM failed to converge, so no realistic ECGs were generated; 1024x1024 grids need ~12 GB GPU and 3 h/epoch (batch 2) vs 1.5 GB, 20 min at 128x128. No quantitative fidelity, distribution or utility metric is reported for any method.

title: Improving Diagnostic Performance through Synthetic Beat Generation: A Hybrid Framework Combining Undersampling and Generative Oversampling for Balanced ECG Learning
authors: Ruby Narula; Neha Goyal
venue: IEEE Global Conference for Advancement in Technology (GCAT)
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP, Conv1DTranspose generator from 100-d noise + 1D-CNN critic) + NearMiss undersampling
task: augmentation (class-balanced beats, 5 classes; separate per-class generation)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (preprocessed 187-sample beat version, 87,553 beats - matches the Kaggle/Kachuee heartbeat dataset)
fs_hz: not reported (187-sample Kaggle/Kachuee beats are 125 Hz)
signal_length_s: not reported (187 samples per beat, ~1.5 s at 125 Hz)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP critic/generator losses (Wasserstein + gradient penalty)
eval_metrics: downstream RBF-SVM accuracy, precision, recall, F1 (overall and per class), confusion matrix; no signal-level metrics
notes: Imbalanced SVM: acc 0.98, macro F1 0.89 (class 1 and 3 recall 0.66); 'balanced' (NearMiss + WGAN-GP, 50,000 beats) reports 1.00 on every metric and class. The balanced condition appears to be evaluated on a split of the augmented dataset (synthetic beats likely in test), a strong leakage red flag; no direct quality metric of synthetic beats is reported.

title: Improving Diffusion Models for ECG Imputation with an Augmented Template Prior
authors: Alexander Jenkins; Zehua Chen; Fu Siong Ng; Danilo Mandic
model_family: Diffusion (PulseDiff: CSDI and SSSD-S4 backbones conditioned on augmented pulse-template prior)
datasets: PTB-XL (PulseImpute splits: 8730 train / 2176 val / 10931 test)
loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE conditioned on observed values and template prior p
eval_metrics: MSE (imputed vs ground truth); downstream multi-label classification macro-AUC (rhythm, form, diagnostic) with pretrained xResNet1d; beat detection F1, precision, sensitivity (SWT detector, 50 ms tolerance); evaluated at 10-50% missingness (transient and extended)
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: pretrained xResNet1d classifiers from PulseImpute (downstream only)
notes: Follows PulseImpute benchmark. Transient 30%: PulseDiff-SSSDS4 MSE 0.0021; extended: 0.0192, deterministic BDC transformer still best. Notes diffusion trained on noise-space loss underperforms on long gaps.

title: Introducing a Comprehensive Framework for Synthetic ECG Validation
authors: Zanchi B, Monachino G, Metaldi M, Conte G, Meystre S, Faraci FD.
venue: IEEE open journal of engineering in medicine and biology
model_family: EvalOnly (validation framework; applied to Pulse2Pulse GAN Brugada ECGs)
datasets: Private Brugada type-I 12-lead ECGs (21 patients, 1122 10-s windows with 50% overlap) vs 1122 synthetic
loss_functions: n/a (Pulse2Pulse WGAN-GP referenced)
eval_metrics: Four layers: (1) visual inspection; (2) morphology via NeuroKit on lead II: RR, PR, QRS, QT, QTc (Bazett), P/QRS/T axes, Mann-Whitney U; (3) similarity: Euclidean distance, maximum absolute error, cosine similarity, MSE, RMSE, NRMSE, RMSPE, kernel MMD, KL divergence, DTW (KMMD/KL/DTW on II, V1, V2) benchmarked against R-vs-R intra-subject and inter-subject distances; (4) expert cardiologist scoring
notes: Only supplementary text available. Key idea: synthetic-to-real distance should lie between real intra-subject and inter-subject variability (R-vs-R benchmarking). Careful statistics: patient-level median aggregation to respect independence. Mentions EU AI Act/GMLP as validation gate.

title: Invertible Conditional Generative Adversarial Networks to Effectively Generate Myocardial Infarction from Normal ECG
authors: Sara Battiston; Roberto Sassi; Massimo Walter Rivolta
venue: 2025 47th Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
model_family: GAN (Invertible conditional GAN, IcGAN: 2D-conv cGAN + encoder mapping real beat to (z, y); compared with CycleGAN of equal generator size)
task: class-to-class style transfer of 12-lead heartbeats (NORM ↔ ASMI ↔ IMI)
datasets: PTB-XL subset (10,776 ECGs: NORM, ASMI, IMI; 100 Hz; 35,353 beats, patient-wise 70/30 split)
signal_length_s: 0.40 (−100 ms to +300 ms around R, 40 samples)
loss_functions: cGAN adversarial (BCE, sigmoid discriminator); encoder trained with L2 loss to recover (z, y) from 3,000 generated beats; CycleGAN baseline with cycle-consistency
eval_metrics: 90% per-lead confidence bands (2,500 real vs synthetic); 2D UMAP density heatmap of real with synthetic overlay; GAN-train and GAN-test accuracy (ResNet-style CNN, 3 classes); per-lead ST-segment (80 ms) mean amplitude comparison with modified Hotelling T² simultaneous 95% CIs
notes: IcGAN GAN-test 84% (baseline 90%), GAN-train 73% (baseline 100%) vs CycleGAN 74%/60%, i.e. synthetic data form a narrower sub-distribution; ST-amplitude CIs include zero in 4/12 leads (synthetic ASMI) and 2/12 (synthetic NORM), mean differences −0.014 to 0.050 mV, below the 0.1 mV STEMI threshold. Evaluation is unpaired/distributional on transferred test beats; GAN-train/test baselines and splits differ (synthetic 21,212 vs real 10,606), no expert review, and no check that patient-specific features are preserved beyond visual examples.

title: Investigating Transformer-Based GANs for Realistic ECG Time-Series Data Generation
authors: Gabriel B. Moro; Joaquim Assunção; Isabel Cristina Reinheimer; Carlos Eduardo Poli‐de‐Figueiredo; Luís A. L. Silva
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS)
model_family: GAN (TTS-CGAN: Transformer-encoder generator, ViT-style patch-embedding Transformer discriminator with adversarial + class heads; LSGAN loss, DiffAug, EMA)
task: class-cond (MIT-BIH 5 beat classes; MIMIC-IV heart-rate trend classes low/normal/high) + retraining the GAN on hybrid real/synthetic sets
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (pre-processed 187-sample heartbeat version); MIMIC-IV (hourly charted heart-rate values, not ECG waveforms)
n_leads: 1 (MIT-BIH beats); MIMIC-IV series are heart-rate values, not ECG leads
fs_hz: not reported (187-sample MIT-BIH beats; MIMIC-IV resampled to 1 sample/hour)
signal_length_s: not reported (MIT-BIH 187 samples per beat; MIMIC-IV 120-232 hourly steps)
loss_functions: Least-squares GAN loss for G and D, plus discriminator class-classification head
eval_metrics: DTW on example real/synthetic pairs; PCA and t-SNE plots; mean cosine similarity; Jensen-Shannon distance (per class); heatmap visual comparison; same metrics after retraining the GAN on hybrid datasets with 20/40/60/100% synthetic
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (cosine/JS computed on raw normalised sequences)
notes: Cosine similarity 0.84 (non-ectopic) to 0.99 (MIMIC-IV HR classes), JS distance 0.12-0.24; example-pair DTW 0.17-0.26 (MIT-BIH) and 0.10-0.13 (MIMIC-IV). Despite the abstract, the 'hybrid' experiment retrains the GAN itself on mixed data and re-measures cosine/JS (up to 60% synthetic keeps metrics stable); no downstream classifier is trained. MIMIC-IV part models hourly heart-rate trends, not ECG; exact cosine/JS construction is not specified.

title: L2L-ESN: A Lead-to-Lead Electrocardiogram Synthesis Network for Assisting Myocardial Infarction Diagnosis
authors: Jian Tan; Xinrui Qiu; Zhanshuo Shang; Xunhua Huang; Haoyi Fan; Zongmin Wang
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP; 1D U-Net multihead generator with one output channel per target lead; 1D CNN critic on concatenated source+target leads)
task: lead reconstruction (II→7 key leads '1T7'; II+V1→6 key leads '2T6'; remaining 4 limb leads derived) + MI detection/localisation
datasets: PTB-XL (5486 MI: 3078 AMI, 3271 IMI); HeMI (private, Zhengzhou University; 26602 MI records: 8190 AMI, 9157 IMI)
n_leads: 1 or 2 in -> 7 or 6 generated (8 independent leads; III, aVR, aVL, aVF derived) -> 12
loss_functions: conditional Wasserstein adversarial loss with gradient penalty (lambda_GP 10, n_critic 5) + MSE reconstruction (lambda_MSE:lambda_CWGAN = 50:1)
eval_metrics: RMSE; Pearson correlation (PCC); discrete curve Fréchet distance (FD) (mean±SD, MI vs non-MI); per-lead binary MI detection precision/recall/F1 using synthesized vs real lead; MI detection with limited real + synthetic lead combinations; AMI/IMI localisation P/R/F1; baselines SSSD-S4, ecg_recon, lead_recon with training time; ablations (multihead vs single-head, loss variants, loss-weight grid); deployment profiling (params, size FP32/FP16/INT8, FLOPs, GPU latency, peak memory); qualitative plots
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (FD is curve-based on raw signals)
notes: 1T7 PTB-XL: RMSE 0.158, PCC 0.747, FD 0.739 vs SSSD-S4 0.163/0.737/0.825; 2T6 non-MI PCC 0.823 (PTB-XL), 0.846 (HeMI); MI harder than non-MI. Synthesized single leads give MI-detection F1 close to but below real leads (e.g. PTB-XL V2 80.5 vs 83.5); II+V1+III(syn) F1 84.8 vs II+V1 real 83.9. Generator 4.95 M params, 4.46 ms GPU. All similarity metrics paired; per-sample PCC SD ~0.2-0.3 shows large variance; 'expert judgment' visualisation is only figures; HeMI private.

title: Latent diffusion based hard sample generation for obstructive sleep apnea detection using single-lead ECG
authors: Yue Li; Mikhail Gur'evich Poluektov; Álan Luiz Éckeli; Yuan Zhang; Hung-Chun Li
model_family: Diffusion (latent feature diffusion model integrated with BAFNet)
datasets: PhysioNet Apnea-ECG
loss_functions: unknown (abstract only)
eval_metrics: downstream OSA detection accuracy; sensitivity; F1-score
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: BAFNet latent features (generation in feature space)
notes: Generates feature vectors (not waveforms) for hard samples near decision boundary; evaluated only by downstream classifier gains.

title: Leveraging Statistical Shape Priors in GAN-Based ECG Synthesis
authors: Nour Neifar; Achraf Ben Hamadou; Afef Mdhaffar; Mohamed Jmaïel; Bernd Freisleben
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP generating statistical shape model parameters; 2D shape prior of temporal+amplitude variation; DTW-based k-means; LSTM discriminator)
task: class-cond (heartbeat classes N, V, F); augmentation
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII)
signal_length_s: single heartbeat, 270 samples (350 ms pre / 400 ms post R-peak)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (Wasserstein adversarial + gradient penalty, lambda=10)
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; MSE; Earth Mover's Distance (EMD); DTW (ms); downstream precision/recall/F1 of three heartbeat classifiers in 5 augmentation settings; cardiologist visual Turing test (3 cardiologists, real vs synthetic and class identification)
notes: Includes useful literature table of metrics used by prior ECG GANs (MMD, DTW, FD, PRD, RMSE, PCC, DTW_D, MVDTW). Cardiologists recognized ~90-96.6% of real beats as real and classified synthetic classes correctly. Class F F1 rose to 0.93 with augmentation.

title: Lightweight Multi-task CNN for ECG Diagnosis with GRU-Diffusion
authors: Lehuai Xu; Zirui Lu; Haoran Yang; Yina Zhou
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM U-Net with embedded 16-layer GRU, 'GRU-Diffusion') + lightweight multi-task CNN classifier (DFNet)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (12 classes); PTB Diagnostic ECG Database (9 classes, 12 standard leads)
loss_functions: Generator: standard DDPM objective (not explicitly stated); classifier: cross-entropy for two tasks + L2 regularization
eval_metrics: FID (Fréchet distance on PCA-reduced signals); mean and std of DTW on randomly paired real/generated signals; KL divergence between Welch PSDs; downstream Accuracy, Precision, Recall, F1; params/FLOPs
notes: 'FID' computed on PCA features of raw signals, not an Inception/ECG network - naming inconsistency. Reports 99.72% (MIT-BIH) and 99.89% (PTB) accuracy. Uses both mean and std of random-pair DTW as diversity/alignment indicator.

title: MAGIC: Multi-Grained Conditional Diffusion for High-Fidelity PPG-to-ECG Translation
authors: Huixiang Wen; Shan Chang; Luo Zhou; Wei Liu; Jiaming Pei; Shengqun Jiang
venue: IEEE journal of biomedical and health informatics
model_family: Diffusion (1D Diffusion Transformer, v-prediction, cosine schedule T=500, classifier-free guidance w=3.5; PPG Transformer encoder with 4 global tokens via AdaLN + token-wise gated cross-attention; encoder pre-trained against paired ECG teacher)
datasets: WESAD; DaLiA; BIDMC; MIMIC-AFib (118 subjects total); downstream: PPG-BP (diabetes), Cuffless-BP (blood pressure)
signal_length_s: 4 (512-sample windows; 8-s windows for HR, 2-s for diabetes, 10-s for BP)
loss_functions: diffusion v-prediction MSE; encoder pre-training: ROI-weighted (R-peak +-32 samples) ECG reconstruction MSE + InfoNCE contrastive PPG-ECG loss + stop-gradient latent alignment loss
eval_metrics: FD (Fréchet distance in learned feature space, RDDM protocol); RMSE (paired); HR MAE via Hamilton detector; AFib accuracy/F1 (VGG-13 on STFT spectrograms, pretrained on real MIMIC-AFib ECG); diabetes detection accuracy/F1 (VGG-11, PPG-BP); SBP/DBP MAE (1D-UNet on PPG + generated ECG); inference time vs steps; prediction-type and component ablations; qualitative visualisation
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: not specified (FD 'in a learned feature space' following RDDM evaluation protocol)
notes: FD at T=500: MAGIC vs RDDM 2.88 vs 8.80 (WESAD), 0.52 vs 2.93 (DaLiA), 2.02 vs 6.54 (BIDMC), 0.69 vs 6.42 (MIMIC-AFib); RMSE mixed (0.16-0.27, RDDM better on several settings); HR MAE 3.28 / 4.74 bpm (WESAD/DaLiA); AFib acc 0.661 vs real ECG 0.706 (F1 0.675 vs RDDM 0.681); DBP MAE 1.34 vs 1.55 mmHg. Authors candidly note no significance testing, no multi-seed analysis, no cardiologist review, ROI mask needs ground-truth ECG, and that the FD feature extractor follows RDDM without specification; train/test subject split not described, so subject leakage cannot be ruled out.

title: MedFlow: Class-Aware Multi-Scale Generation for Medical Time-Series Synthesis
authors: Yanhao Huang; Shibo Feng; Wanjin Feng; Peilin Zhao; Chunyan Miao
model_family: FlowMatching (class-aware multi-scale flow matching over VQ multi-scale token embeddings with Token Marginal Guidance; MedFlow)
task: class-cond (medical time series incl. ECG; imbalanced classes)
datasets: MIMIC-III; eICU (EHR); APAVA (EEG); PTB Diagnostic ECG (Medformer split, 108/29/61 subjects)
loss_functions: Stage 1 tokenizer: MSE reconstruction + cosine commitment loss (EMA codebooks); Stage 2: categorical endpoint cross-entropy loss (class-weighted) + structured-source prior regularizer (no direct velocity regression)
eval_metrics: TSTR AUROC; TSTR AUPRC; Discriminative Score (post-hoc GRU); Predictive Score; Context-FID (TS2Vec encoder, dim 320); t-SNE overlap; feature-wise moment, tail-quantile and minority-class statistic discrepancies; sampling throughput
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: TS2Vec encoder fitted on real data (Context-FID); GRU for discriminative/predictive scores
notes: For PTB ECG only TSTR AUROC/AUPRC reported; DS/PS/C-FID reported for EHR tasks. Claims avg -88.6% C-FID and 3.8x throughput vs TarDiff. Emphasises that global fidelity metrics can hide minority-class/tail failures.

title: Minority class-aware multiclass arrhythmia detection using conditional GAN augmentation
authors: Tiwari A, Kishore J, Singh R.
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP with auxiliary classifier in critic; 1D transposed-conv generator)
task: class-cond / augmentation (minority S and F beats)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI 5 classes N, S, V, F, Q)
loss_functions: Wasserstein adversarial loss + gradient penalty + auxiliary classifier (cross-entropy) loss in critic; downstream classifier cross-entropy
eval_metrics: DTW; SSIM (synthetic vs real beats); visual P-QRS-T inspection; downstream hierarchical multi-stream / ResNet34 classifier accuracy, per-class and macro F1, per-class AUC/ROC, 5-fold cross-validation; inference latency, GFLOPs, memory, power on Jetson Nano/Raspberry Pi 5
notes: Augmenting S and F to 10,000 each: macro F1 0.78 -> 0.94, F-class F1 +38%, S +28%. GAN checkpoint chosen by lowest critic loss and best downstream macro F1 on validation (selection on utility). Fidelity metrics (DTW, SSIM) only briefly reported.

title: MM-DADM: Multimodal Drug-Aware Diffusion Model for Virtual Clinical Trials
authors: Qian Shao; Bang Du; Zepeng Li; Qiyuan Chen; Jiahe Chen; Hongxia Xu; Jimeng Sun; Jian Wu; Jintai Chen
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM backbone with pharmacokinetic ODE fusion via dynamic cross-attention + counterfactual drug-aware ControlNet-style CDC-Net; contrastive causal feature encoder)
task: other-modality2ECG / class-cond (drug- and demographics-conditioned post-dose ECG from pre-dose ECG; virtual clinical trials)
datasets: ECGRDVQ and ECGDMMLD (FDA drug trials; 9,443 12-lead ECGs, 44 subjects, 8 regimens)
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; 4 limb leads derived)
loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE (L_bb, L_real) + lambda*causal guidance loss L_cau (1 - cosine sim to drug prototypes, lambda=0.1) for counterfactual samples; supervised contrastive loss L_con for the causal feature encoder
eval_metrics: accuracy/recall of normal-vs-abnormal status agreement on QTc (Bazett), PR, Tpeak-Tend intervals (single and multi-indicator); Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD); RMSE; cardiologist real-vs-generated discrimination accuracy (10 cardiologists, 100 ECGs per lead per method); downstream ResNet-1D drug-administration classification with 100/200/500 synthetic augmentations
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: 1D ResNet pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (final FC layer output) for FRD
notes: FRD 0.2431, RMSE 0.0127 vs SSSD-ECG 0.4719/0.0312 and FlowECG 0.5164. Expert Turing test: ideal is ~50% accuracy; MM-DADM near chance. Clinical-interval threshold agreement (normal/abnormal) is a novel clinically-grounded metric. Compares 10 baselines.

title: MorphDiff-ECG: A Diffusion Model for Multimodal Feature Fusion of ECG Signals
authors: Lei Zhang; Cheng Su; Mengying Ou; Mengyue Wang; Zhichao Xu; Shiyu Wei; Chang Liu; Tao Lei; Yong Wan
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, x0-prediction; Transformer encoder + Feature Decoupling Enhancement with trend (polynomial), periodic (CWT top-M) and morphology (opening/closing) branches + SE-attention fusion; classifier-guided conditional sampling)
