authors: Debaditya Shome; Pritam Sarkar; Ali Etemad
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
model_family: Diffusion (RDDM: region-disentangled DDPM with ROI (QRS)-guided forward process, two denoisers)
datasets: WESAD; DALIA; CAPNO; BIDMC; MIMIC-AFib (training); CardioBench: WESAD, DALIA, MIMIC-AFib, PPG-BP, Cuffless-BP
loss_functions: lambda1*||mu*eps - eps_theta(x_t^m,c,t)||^2 (ROI/QRS noise) + lambda2*||x_t^m - rho_phi(x_t,c,t)||^2 (non-ROI denoising)
eval_metrics: RMSE; Fréchet Distance (FD, following CardioGAN); CardioBench: HR estimation MAE (bpm, Hamilton detector), AFib detection F1/accuracy, stress and affect classification F1/accuracy, diabetes detection, SBP/DBP estimation MAE (train on real, test on generated)
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (FD computed on signals following CardioGAN)
notes: Introduces CardioBench: train-on-real/test-on-generated downstream benchmark with real-test performance as upper bound. Only 10 sampling steps. Subject-independent evaluation.

title: ReHeartNet: Reconstruct Electrocardiogram From Photoplethysmography by Using Dense Connected Deep Learning Model
authors: Shuenn-Yuh Lee; Kai-Ze Lei; Ju-Yi Chen; CHUN-RONG HUANG
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology
model_family: Other (deterministic regression: densely connected BiLSTM, DC-BiLSTM); baselines GAN (CardioGAN), BiLSTM, Transformer
datasets: MIMIC-III; BIDMC; TBME-RR; CBIC-Heart (new long-term dataset)
fs_hz: varies per dataset (not unified in text)
loss_functions: RMSE reconstruction loss
eval_metrics: RMSE; Pearson correlation r; beat-timing error (mean absolute R-peak displacement, Pan-Tompkins, nearest-peak matching without tolerance window); 95% CIs across subjects; significance tests vs baselines
notes: Introduces beat-timing error since amplitude metrics miss R-peak displacement critical for HR/HRV. Cross-dataset sampling-rate differences used to test robustness.

title: Semi-supervised GAN for enhancing electrocardiogram time series diagnostics
authors: Dawei Li; Tienan Chen; Cong Liu; Liqi Liao; Shaoping Chen; Yongqiang Cui; Li Zhang; Yiyu Shi; Xiaowei Xu
model_family: GAN (TimeGAN-style: RNN embedding/recovery autoencoder + RNN generator and bidirectional RNN discriminator in latent space; GRU / LSTM / LSTM-LN cells)
task: class-wise synthesis for augmentation / class balancing (RBBB, RVOT, LVOT, Brugada, normal)
datasets: Private: Guangdong Provincial People's Hospital, 653 patients (553 train / 100 test, 20 per class), ECG records described as waveform graphs
n_leads: not reported (12-lead source; class-specific leads V1/V2/V5/V6 used for diagnosis)
signal_length_s: 13.89 stated for generated signals; classifier uses first 3600 samples (10 s)
loss_functions: autoencoder reconstruction loss + unsupervised adversarial (BCE) loss in latent space + supervised next-step latent prediction loss (the 'semi-supervised' part)
eval_metrics: t-SNE and PCA real vs synthetic; discriminative score (post-hoc RNN real-vs-synthetic classifier accuracy); predictive score (MAE of next-step predictor trained on synthetic, tested on real); ResNet-18 1D classification test accuracy, sensitivity, specificity (per class) with real, real+synthetic, synthetic-only training; comparison vs random oversampling, RCGAN, GES, Nef-Net
notes: Discriminative score 0.179 (GRU) / 0.238 (LSTM) / 0.193 (LSTM-LN), predictive MAE 0.022-0.027. Augmentation: Real 200 → Real+Syn 100+100 GRU accuracy 91.25 → 94.04%; synthetic-only 1000 GRU samples (TSTR) 97.2% vs real-553 92.1%, RCGAN 92.8%, GES 95.2%. Despite the title, this is a TimeGAN-like model, not a discriminator-as-classifier SGAN. Caveats: tiny private test set (100 records), patient counts inconsistent (653 vs 833), synthetic-only outperforming real is unexplained; no waveform or clinical fidelity metrics.

title: Shape and amplitude decoupling in pulsatile physiological signal synthesis and its evaluation
authors: Kim J, Park K, Chen L, Kim K.
model_family: VAE (VABAM: variational framework with cascaded HPF/LPF filtering, bidirectional GRU, Gaussian shape latent z + uniform amplitude parameter theta); baselines ConVAE, FactorVAE, TCVAE, VDVAE, DiffWave, VDWave, WaveNet
task: other (amplitude-controllable synthesis with shape-amplitude decoupling; frequency-cutoff conditioning)
datasets: MIMIC-III Waveform (ABP and ECG); VitalDB (ABP and ECG); cross-dataset train/test
loss_functions: ELBO with four terms: signal reconstruction log p(y|x); feature-subset reconstruction log p(x|z,theta) vs q(x|y,theta); KL(q(z|y)||N(0,I)); KL(q(theta|y)||Uniform) relaxed via reparameterized Bernoulli
eval_metrics: Five metrics: waveform shape factorization (SF), shape preservation / spectral distortion (SP/SD), amplitude modulation controllability (AC), spectral similarity (via conditional mutual information / KL on PSD permutation densities using FFT, DCT, Welch), reconstruction R2; composite ISCORE (arithmetic/geometric/harmonic mean of normalized metrics, Linfoot informational correlation normalisation)
notes: Nature Communications evaluation-oriented paper: introduces CMI-based PSD metrics and an aggregate ISCORE; shows ranking depends on PSD estimator (FFT/DCT/Welch) and aggregation mean, so they report all. SF excluded for non-factorized models (diffusion). 400k/50k/20k train/val/test per signal/dataset.

title: Simulator and Experience Enhanced Diffusion Model for Comprehensive ECG Generation
authors: Xiaoda Wang; Kaiqiao Han; Yuhao Xu; Xiao Luo; Yizhou Sun; Wei Wang; Carl Yang
model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM in VAE latent space, ODE-simulator-enhanced, LLM-powered EHR retrieval; 'SE-Diff')
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (800,035 ECGs); MIMIC-IV-Clinical (EHR retrieval)
loss_functions: VAE: full reconstruction + β-KL + beat-decoder loss + log-spectrum (rFFT) band-weighted spectral loss; Diffusion: L_DDPM + λ simulator-guided Euler ODE-consistency loss + γ inter-lead (Einthoven/Goldberger) consistency loss
eval_metrics: Per-lead MAE; NRMSE; Pearson r; HR MAE (MAE_HR); relative CLIP score (rCLIP = s(gen,text)/s(real,text)); relative FID (rFID = FID(gen,real)/FID(real split1, real split2)) in ECG embedding space; downstream F1, Accuracy, AUROC for imbalanced sex and SVT classification
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: ECG encoder of a CLIP-style ECG-text model (specific model not named)
notes: Normalising FID and CLIP by real-vs-real reference values controls for encoder bias - a good practice. Physics losses include Einthoven/Goldberger inter-lead identity constraints. Only baseline is DiffuSETS.

title: Single-Lead ECG Arrhythmia Classification Based on Peak-Enhanced Attention Network and Quality-Aware GAN Data Augmentation Framework
authors: Zhang Y, Xia Y.
model_family: GAN (Quality-Aware GAN, QA-GAN: CNN + BiLSTM, kurtosis-based dynamic soft-label discriminator)
datasets: PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (AliveCor, 8,528 recordings); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (classifier adaptability)
loss_functions: Generator: standard adversarial loss; Discriminator: dynamic soft-label BCE with real-sample target y = α + (1−α)·tanh(log(K(x)+1)/5) from signal kurtosis K (α=0.7 best)
eval_metrics: visual comparison; t-SNE overlap of real vs synthetic AF features; downstream classifier precision, sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, F1, macro-F1, AUC/ROC, PR curves; comparison vs SMOTE, random oversampling, class-weighted loss; noise robustness
notes: Generator quality evaluated only visually and via downstream augmentation (F1 0.793 baseline → 0.816 with QA-GAN vs 0.809 class-weighted loss). Kurtosis used as a signal-quality index during training — could also serve as an SQI metric for synthetic ECGs.

title: SMA-GAN: A Physiology-Guided Adversarial Network with Attention and Spectral Constraints for Imbalanced ECG Synthesis
authors: Jiaqi Liang; Ruizhe Wang; Zhanyi Liu; Honghao Li; Yujie Ma; Min Xiang
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing (ICASSP 2026)
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP, 1D transposed-conv generator with Physiology-Guided Modulation Attention on QRS + FFT spectral consistency loss; conv critic)
task: class-cond / augmentation (minority F-class heartbeat synthesis, one model per class)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI 5 classes, patient-independent split: 87,550 train / 21,888 test beats; 642 F beats)
n_leads: 1 (single heartbeat channel; MIT-BIH is 2-lead, lead used not stated)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP critic/generator loss (lambda_gp=10); spectral consistency L1 loss on FFT magnitude between real and generated beats (lambda_spec=1.0)
eval_metrics: MSE; PRD; DTW; SSIM; FD-SIM (Fréchet-distance-based similarity); downstream 1D-CNN classification on MIT-BIH with 3000/5000 synthetic F beats added: F1 of F class, balanced accuracy, G-mean, macro F1; ablation (PGMA, spectral loss)
notes: SMA-GAN (5000 synth F beats): MSE 0.003, PRD 10.5%, DTW 0.034, SSIM 0.632, FD-SIM 0.999; F1-F 0.498 (no augmentation) -> 0.863, macro F1 0.837 -> 0.954 vs WGAN-GP 0.828/0.943. Pairing of synthetic vs real beats for MSE/PRD/DTW/SSIM is not described, FD-SIM's feature space is undefined and saturates (0.93-0.999 for every method), and results are single runs without variance; patient-independent split is a plus.

title: Spatially-Conditioned Variational Autoencoder with Latent Manifold Harvesting for High-Fidelity 12-Lead ECG Synthesis
authors: Ashutosh Mishra; Nicolas Stein; Louis Peter; Michael Guckert
model_family: VAE (spatially-conditioned cVAE with multi-resolution beat-position mask injection, nearest-neighbour upsampling; Latent Manifold Harvesting latent bank)
task: class-cond (major pathology + comorbidity profile; beat-position mask)
datasets: Large 12-lead ECG database v1.0.0 (Chapman-Shaoxing/Ningbo, 45,152 patients, SNOMED-CT codes)
loss_functions: MSE reconstruction + KL divergence (standard VAE ELBO)
eval_metrics: visual side-by-side inspection; per-channel 1D-ResNet ensemble classifier applied to synthetic ECGs: Pearson correlation between predicted pathology prevalence and training distribution ('Ensemble Correlation'); Cumulative Mean Certainty / Reliability Score (mean |p-0.5|*2); reconstruction MSE; heuristic peak-alignment acceptance criteria
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: per-channel 1D-ResNet classifiers trained on real data
notes: Latent Manifold Harvesting: only latents whose decodings pass R-peak count/location/amplitude and baseline-smoothness tolerance are banked, then jittered (rejection sampling biases diversity). Per-lead independent VAEs ignore inter-lead consistency. Ensemble correlation r>=0.98 for AFIB, LBBB, AF; 100 samples per pathology; CPU-only training.

title: SSSD-ECG-nle: New Label Embeddings with Structured State-Space Models for ECG generation
authors: Sergey Skorik; Aram Avetisyan
model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG with new label embeddings 'nle': separate embeddings for label presence/absence; S4 backbone)
datasets: PTB-XL (folds 1-8 train, 9 val, 10 test)
loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction MSE
eval_metrics: TSTR and TRTS with xResNet1d50 (binary per pathology: AFIB, CRBBB, PVC, 1AVB, CLBBB): G-mean, F1-score; multilabel TSTR/TRTS weighted G-mean, F1, ROC-AUC; real-data augmentation with synthetic positives; convergence analysis over training checkpoints; physician evaluation: text-report diagnosis accuracy on 100 real + 100 synthetic, and direct real-vs-synthetic discrimination (380 ECGs) confusion matrix
code_available: https://github.com/ispras/EcgLib (synthetic data and physician evaluations released)
notes: Key pitfall: good TSTR yet physicians identified synthetic ECGs almost perfectly (279/280 synthetic, 99/100 real correct); cues were low voltage, apparently reversed chest electrodes, artefacts. Authors dropped relation metrics (DTW, MMD, Wasserstein) and TSTS as 'uninformative'.

title: Style translation of simulated ECGs to realistic ECGs with generative adversarial networks for data-scarce clinical settings: challenges and opportunities
authors: J Hesp; Wouter A. C. van Amsterdam; Maarten van Smeden
model_family: GAN (CycleGAN style transfer simulated->realistic ECG)
datasets: PTB-XL (987 ECGs, 56 RBBB); MedalCareXL simulations (25 RBBB)
loss_functions: CycleGAN adversarial + cycle-consistency (implied by CycleGAN; not detailed)
eval_metrics: Downstream RBBB classifier AUC; average precision (AP) for real-only, real+raw simulations, real+translated simulations
notes: Conference abstract. Raw simulations harmed (AUC 0.93, AP 0.68); translated restored to baseline (AUC 0.95 vs 0.96, AP 0.81 vs 0.79). Notes clinicians recognise synthetic style; argues diffusion models offer objective convergence diagnostics vs unstable GANs.

title: Synthesis of Multimodal Cardiological Signals Using a Conditional Wasserstein Generative Adversarial Network
authors: Ioana Crețu; Alexander Tindale; Wamadeva Balachandran; Maysam Abbod; Ashraf William Khir; Hongying Meng
model_family: GAN (MC-WGAN: conditional WGAN-GP, 1D U-Net generator with 6 down/6 up blocks and label embedding, 6-layer 1D-conv critic)
task: class-cond multimodal beat synthesis (ECG + ABP + CVP jointly; rhythm classes N, F, T, L, paced P); ECG-only on MIT-BIH for benchmarking
datasets: Private Harefield Hospital ICU dataset (29 patients, PACESIM trial: ECG V1 + invasive ABP + CVP, sinus/AF/AT/LBBB/paced); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (lead II, AAMI classes N, A, V, R, L)
n_leads: 1 ECG lead (V1 private; MLII MIT-BIH) + 2 pressure channels (ABP, CVP)
signal_length_s: 0.8 (single beat: ECG centred on R, ABP/CVP -200/+600 ms); ~0.71 (MIT-BIH, 88+168 samples)
loss_functions: Conditional Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty (λ=10), 5:1 critic:generator updates
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; MSE; PRD; discrete curve Fréchet distance; DTW; MMD (Gaussian kernel) — each generated beat vs all real beats, averaged; per class and per signal; comparison with published MIT-BIH numbers (SynSigGAN, BC-GAN, BiLSTM-CNN GAN, Transformer-GAN, 2D WGAN); visual comparison
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (all metrics on raw normalised beats)
notes: Private data, all signals/classes: RMSE 0.319, PRD 33.2, FD 0.490, DTW 3.27, MMD 0.469; ECG RMSE 0.248, PRD 25.1; CVP worst (PRD 48.3). MIT-BIH: RMSE 0.205, MAE 0.146, PRD 20.5, FD 0.225, DTW 1.355, MMD 0.0051 vs BC-GAN PRD 33.8, SynSigGAN PRD 6.3. Distances are averaged over all real beats (not nearest neighbour), cross-paper comparisons use different protocols, and no cross-modal consistency (e.g. ECG-ABP pulse transit delay), diversity or utility evaluation is done despite the multimodal claim.

title: Synthetic artificial intelligence in cardiology: from generative models to clinical applications
authors: Gianmarco Parise; Roberto Ceravolo; Fabiana Lucà; Michele Massimo Gulizia; Cecilia Tetta; Orlando Parise; Federico Nardi; Massimo Grimaldi; Sandro Gelsomino
model_family: Survey (GANs, VAEs, Diffusion, Transformers, Autoregressive models, Digital Twins, Synthetic Cohort Simulators in cardiology)
datasets: not applicable (mentions synthetic 12-lead ECG from electrophysiological simulations, DeepFake ECG)
loss_functions: described conceptually only: adversarial training (generator vs discriminator); variational/probabilistic latent modelling; progressive denoising (diffusion)
eval_metrics: no specific quantitative metric catalogue; calls for standardized evaluation frameworks, clinical relevance validation, traceability/auditing, clinician validation of realism, logical consistency and population representativeness (TIMA framework: coverage, novelty, coherence); privacy preservation; bias/under-representation checks
notes: Clinician-oriented state-of-the-art review (Eur Heart J Open). Identifies lack of standardized evaluation frameworks and labelling as a key risk; recommends embedding clinicians in validation (TIMA). ECG coverage is brief; few concrete metrics.

title: Synthetic Data Generation via Generative Adversarial Networks in Healthcare: A Systematic Review of Image- and Signal-Based Studies
authors: Muhammed Halil Akpınar; Abdulkadir Şengür; Massimo Salvi; Silvia Seoni; Oliver Faust; Hasan Mir; Filippo Molinari; U. Rajendra Acharya
venue: IEEE Open Journal of Engineering in Medicine and Biology
model_family: Survey (GANs in healthcare, image and signal; PRISMA, 72 studies)
datasets: catalogued: various (MRI, CT, ECG incl. MIT-BIH, PTB-XL etc.)
loss_functions: Catalogues GAN architectures (cGAN 31%, CycleGAN 18%, Pix2Pix, StyleGAN, PGGAN, SynSigGAN, DC-WGAN); minimax adversarial and cycle-consistency losses
eval_metrics: Catalogued: PSNR; SSIM; MAE; FID; Dice; NMSE; RMSE; AUC; accuracy/sensitivity/specificity; image Turing test
notes: Signal section is thin (ECG: SynSigGAN low FID/RMSE; SSSD-ECG high AUC). Main finding: no standardized metrics, SSIM/PSNR miss clinical significance; recommends no-reference metrics usable also as losses.

title: Synthetic ECG Generation for Data Augmentation and Transfer Learning in Arrhythmia Classification
authors: José Fernando Núñez; Jamie Arjona; Javier Béjar
model_family: Diffusion (DiffWave/SSSD-ECG; Time-Diffusion = HF Diffusers Unet1D conditional) + VQ-VAE/MaskGIT (Time-VQVAE, TimeVQVAE)
datasets: PTB-XL; Chapman-Shaoxing; merged PTB-XL+Chapman (7 rhythm classes: SBRAD, SR, AFIB, STACH, AFLT, SARRH, SVTAC)
loss_functions: not detailed; uses original models' objectives (DiffWave variational bound / diffusion noise prediction; VQ-VAE + MaskGIT prior)
eval_metrics: t-SNE, UMAP, PaCMAP visualisations; 2-sample classifier test (real-vs-synthetic accuracy, 50% ideal); MMD (RBF); TrRTeR, TrSTeS, TrSTeR (TSTR), TrRTeS (TRTS), TrRSTeR (augmentation) with accuracy, precision, recall, F1, ROC AUC (n=25 repeats); fine-tuning transferability with 20-80% real data
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (MMD on data); 1D ResNet-like CNN classifier for TSTR/TRTS
notes: Key criticism: MMD and t-SNE/UMAP visualisations failed to distinguish synthetic from real, while classifier-based tests (2-sample test, TSTR/TRTS) revealed clear differences. Augmentation gains negligible per dataset, positive on merged set. Time-VQVAE best for fine-tuning but still below real-only.

title: Synthetic ECG signal generation using generative neural networks
authors: Edmond Adib; Fatemeh Afghah; John Jeffery Prevost
model_family: GAN (comparison of 5 models: Classic FC GAN, DC-DC GAN, BiLSTM-DC GAN, AE/VAE-DC GAN hybrid, WGAN)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Normal beats, lead I; N vs LBBB for augmentation test)
loss_functions: Binary cross-entropy adversarial loss (all models); AE/VAE-DC GAN: weighted sum of adversarial loss + L1 reconstruction loss; WGAN loss for WGAN model
eval_metrics: DTW, Frechet and Euclidean distances to template; Method 1 mean all-pairs set distance; Method 2/3 distances to random or expert-selected template (min distance); Method 4 productivity rate (% accepted beats under distance threshold); Method 5 expert visual inspection; ResNet34 augmentation precision/recall/F1/accuracy and confusion matrices
notes: Introduces threshold, accepted beat, productivity rate concepts. Euclidean distance unsuitable: a beat with minimum Euclidean distance lacked all morphological features. DTW and discrete Frechet agree; Frechet is a true metric. Classic GAN 72.3% productivity (DTW). Template choice (SAB vs expert-picked) affects scores. Includes table of prior ECG-GAN metrics.

title: Synthetic ECG signals generation: A scoping review
authors: Beatrice Zanchi; Giuliana Monachino; Luigi Fiorillo; Giulio Conte; Angelo Auricchio; Athina Tzovara; Francesca D. Faraci
model_family: Survey (79 studies to Jan 2024: mathematical modelling — physiological, morphological, dynamic/ECGSYN; computer-vision-inherited augmentation — geometric, jitter, warping, filtering; deep generative models — VAEs, vanilla/recurrent/DC/conditional/progressive GANs, VAE-GAN hybrids, diffusion)
datasets: 79 reviewed studies (Web of Science search, 823 hits); datasets catalogued include MIT-BIH Arrhythmia, NSRDB, AFDB, NSTDB, PTB-XL, PhysioNet/CinC 2017/2020/2021, CPSC2018, Chapman (CHINA), CCDD, GESUS, CUDB, VFDB, EPHNOGRAM
n_leads: various (single-lead most common; 12-lead mainly from deep generative models; independent vs dependent multi-lead generation discussed)
signal_length_s: various (single beat, multiple beats, fixed-length recordings; MM can produce multi-beat output from a single beat)
loss_functions: not applicable (survey)
eval_metrics: Catalogue (Fig. 13): visual inspection; increase in downstream/auxiliary classifier performance (ICP); MSE-based (MSE, NMSE, RMSE, NRMSE, PRD); MMD-based (MMD, KMMD, KID); FD-based (Fréchet distance, FID); time-warping (DTW, soft-DTW, TWED); Pearson correlation; Euclidean distance; MAE; MRE; SSIM; SNR; relative entropy/KL; EMD; Chamfer distance; t-SNE; statistics of ECG feature distributions (RR, QT, PR, QRS, axes); Poincaré plot; DFA; training-performance metrics (discriminator accuracy, loss convergence); template-based CI/FI comparison; real-vs-noise baselines; GAN-train/GAN-test (TSTR/TRTS); clinical Turing tests
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: not applicable (survey; notes FID/KID used in some studies)
notes: Classifies 79 works by technique, lead count, beat count and purpose; deep generative models are mostly used for augmentation, MM for modelling/device testing, CVIM for fast augmentation. Key evaluation conclusion: no standardized metric set exists, metrics are implemented and paired inconsistently (all-pairs, template-based, real-vs-real baselines), MSE-based metrics dominate followed by MMD, FD and DTW, so cross-study comparison is impossible; calls for pipelines combining quantitative, clinically relevant and expert assessment and for similarity metrics that do not penalise legitimate variability.

title: Synthetic Electrocardiogram Spectrogram Generation Using Generative Adversarial Network‐Based Models: A Comparative Study
authors: Giovanny Barbosa‐Casanova; Norelli Schettini; Winston Percybrooks; Begonya García-Zapirain
model_family: GAN (DCGAN, conditional GAN, WGAN-GP) on 2-D spectrogram images
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (N, L, R, V, A beats grouped into normal/abnormal)
loss_functions: DCGAN: binary cross-entropy adversarial; CGAN: conditional cross-entropy adversarial; WGAN-GP: Wasserstein critic loss + lambda gradient penalty
eval_metrics: FID (Inception-V3 'pre-aux' 768-d layer via pytorch-fid); intra-class SSIM diversity (average/max/min pairwise SSIM among generated, values near 1 = mode collapse); training runtime and GPU memory; downstream 2D-CNN precision, recall, F1, accuracy on GAN-balanced vs imbalanced training sets
notes: Explicit pitfall: pool_3 FID needs >2048 samples (else complex/NaN covariance); switching layer makes FID values non-comparable across works. Pairwise SSIM among synthetic samples used as mode-collapse/diversity detector.

title: Synthetic electrocardiograms for Brugada syndrome: from data generation to expert cardiologists evaluation
authors: Beatrice Zanchi; Giuliana Monachino; Francesca Dalia Faraci; Matteo Metaldi; Pedro Brugada; Georgia Sarquella‐Brugada; Elijah Raphael Behr; Josép Brugada; Lia Crotti; Bernard Belhassen; Giulio Conte
model_family: GAN (Pulse2Pulse)
task: evaluation (expert Turing test of class-specific synthetic ECGs)
datasets: Private: 12-lead ECGs from 21 Brugada syndrome patients (5-min recordings)
loss_functions: not reported (refers to Pulse2Pulse paper)
eval_metrics: Expert visual Turing test by 7 Brugada specialists (>15 y): accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1 (real=positive); two rounds ≥2 h apart; Wilcoxon signed-rank; intra-rater Cohen's kappa
notes: Experts at chance or worse: accuracy 40%/42%, specificity 22%/26%, sensitivity 58%; kappa −0.12 to 0.80. Bias toward calling ECGs real. Same display settings (25 mm/s, 10 mm/mV). Raises disclosure/watermarking concerns.

title: Text-to-ECG: a Framework to Generate 12-Lead ECG from Text Reports
authors: Fabrizio Cattozzo; Sara Battiston; Massimo W. Rivolta; Roberto Sassi
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society. Annual International Conference
model_family: GAN (conditional WGAN-GP; 1D upsample-conv generator, 2D-conv critic; frozen Bio_ClinicalBERT 768-d text embedding + 300-d uniform noise)
task: text-conditional (12-lead single heartbeat from short English diagnosis text; 5 classes NORM, IMI, ASMI, LAFB, LVH)
datasets: PTB-XL (100 Hz version; 29,391 balanced heartbeats; ~25 hand-written English report variants per class)
signal_length_s: 0.5 (single beat, 50 samples: -150 ms to +350 ms around R peak)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP critic loss (lambda=10) + generator Wasserstein loss; Gaussian instance noise (0.001 mV) added to critic inputs
eval_metrics: UMAP projection of real (KDE heatmap) vs synthetic beats per class; GAN-train (TSTR / train-synthetic test-synthetic) and GAN-test (TRTS) per-class F1 and accuracy; per-timepoint 90% confidence-band overlap IoU per lead; visual comparison with cross-correlation-matched real beat
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (UMAP on raw concatenated 12x50 beats); GAN-train/test classifier = Ribeiro et al. 12-lead DNN architecture
notes: GAN-train: classifier trained on synthetic reaches 0.92 accuracy on synthetic but 0.60 on real (IMI F1 0.43) -> limited diversity; GAN-test: real-trained classifier 0.84 on real vs 0.72 on synthetic (ASMI F1 0.55, IMI 0.56); 90% band IoU 0.73-0.80 per class. UMAP shows ASMI samples landing in the IMI region (class confusion). No cardiologist evaluation despite abstract wording; authors note any fixed metric can be gamed and evaluation remains open.

title: Towards High-Fidelity ECG Generation: Evaluation via Quality Metrics and Human Feedback
authors: Maria Mourão Gonçalves Russo; Hugo Filipe Silveira Gamboa
venue: International Joint Conference on Biomedical Engineering Systems and Technologies (BIOSTEC)
model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG: conditional diffusion with S4 layers, hyperparameter-tuned, conditioned on 5 PTB-XL diagnostic superclasses); GAN (1D DC-style CNN GAN, used only to make low-quality Class 2 signals for the quality dataset)
task: class-cond 12-lead generation / evaluation (new sample-level evaluator model + human feedback)
datasets: PTB-XL (via PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2021); custom 4-class Quality Dataset (basic waveforms, GAN outputs, SSSD-ECG outputs, real PTB-XL)
n_leads: 12 (SSSD-ECG generates 8 leads: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 reconstructed)
signal_length_s: 10 (PTB-XL records; GAN outputs 1000 samples per lead)
loss_functions: GAN: binary cross-entropy for generator and discriminator; SSSD-ECG training loss not stated; evaluator classifier: class-weighted cross-entropy
eval_metrics: improved precision; improved recall; density; coverage (k=5, TSFEL features); TSTR; TRTS; TSTS (Random Forest, macro F1); clinician real-vs-synthetic questionnaire with diagnostic class and quality-level follow-ups; evaluator model (5-CNN ensemble assigning 4 quality levels, % predicted Class 4); Pearson correlation of evaluator with precision/recall/density/coverage; evaluator vs. expert agreement
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: TSFEL (statistical, spectral and temporal handcrafted features)
notes: Extracted from the author's Dec 2024 MSc thesis (NOVA Lisbon), the basis of this paper; details may differ from the published version. Best hyperparameters raised mean precision 0.57->0.94, density 0.80->3.85, coverage 0.19->0.89, but recall stayed ~0.03; RF macro-F1: TRTR 56.58%, TRTS 57.03%, TSTR 40.84%, TSTS 78.00%. Majority vote of 3 clinicians judged 8/10 synthetic ECGs as real (2/10 real judged synthetic), but diagnostic labels for synthetic ECGs lacked consensus; evaluator correlated with precision (r=0.88) and density (r=0.72). Extracted from Maria Russo's Dec 2024 NOVA Lisbon MSc thesis, not the 2025 BIOSTEC paper (doi 10.5220/0013400500003911); human evaluation used signals from the original-hyperparameter model.

title: TransDiffECG: Semantically controllable ECG synthesis via transformer-based diffusion modeling
authors: Yuxin Lin; Jing Ma; Suyu Dong; Chaoyu Sun; Wanting Cong; Kuanquan Wang; Gongning Luo; Wei Wang
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM on SSSD-ECG backbone; Transformer encoder/decoder blocks + Semantic ECG Batch Normalization (SPADE-like) conditioning on P/QRS/T segmentation masks)
task: semantic-mask-conditional (fiducial-level control of P/QRS/T placement, heart rate 50-110 bpm, QTc 330-495 ms); augmentation
datasets: QTDB (single-lead); LUDB (12-lead, patient-wise 5-fold CV); AF vs normal classification on LUDB
fs_hz: not reported in main text (QTDB native 250, LUDB native 500)
signal_length_s: not reported in main text (details in supplementary; multi-beat segments)
loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction MSE
eval_metrics: MMD; Pearson correlation (paired with mask-matched ground truth); U-Net P/QRS/T onset/offset precision and recall under AAMI EC57 tolerances for Real->Synthetic and Synthetic->Real segmentation; AF vs normal AUROC with augmentation (XResNet1d50, 5-fold); qualitative controllability of HR and QTc; membership inference attack AUROC; ablation
eval_category_tags: fidelity; distribution; clinical; utility-TSTR; conditional; privacy
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (MMD on normalized raw signals; kernel/features not specified)
notes: LUDB: MMD 3.21e-2 vs DiffECG 3.49e-2, SSSD-ECG 5.74e-2, P2PGAN 24.47e-2; PC 0.6177 vs 0.4866/0.3995. QTDB S->R segmentation ~98% onset/offset precision/recall (real 97-98.6%); AF AUROC 0.9451 with augmentation vs 0.9004 real-only; MIA AUROC 0.49 (QTDB)/0.51 (LUDB). Caveats: baselines were re-conditioned on masks by the authors; PC is computed against the ground-truth record whose mask was used (paired, so it measures conditional reconstruction) and is also misused as a memorization check; HR/QTc controllability shown only visually; no expert review.

title: Transformer-Based Generative Adversarial Network With Multi-Scale Temporal Attention for ECG Synthesis and PQRST Feature Preservation
authors: Ayswarya R Kurup; Mithun Kumar Kar; Madhusudhan Mishra; Soumyabrata Dev; Debanga Raj Neog
model_family: GAN (TransGAN: Transformer generator with temporal self-attention, positional encoding and Swish; hierarchical multi-scale transformer patch discriminator at beat/rhythm/sequence windows; PQRST-constrained loss via adaptive peak detection)
task: unconditional (noise→10 s ECG) for augmentation with class-weighted loss
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; PTB-XL; a simulated ('synthetic') ECG dataset
loss_functions: adversarial BCE + weighted BCE (class-frequency weights) in discriminator + lambda_PQRST x PQRST feature-consistency loss + temporal coherence constraint
eval_metrics: MSE; DTW; Wasserstein distance; PQRST feature accuracy (fraction of beats with PQRST features within tolerance of real); SNR (0.5-40 Hz vs >40 Hz) real vs synthetic; sample entropy, RR-interval CV, QRS-duration CV with paired t-test; magnitude and phase spectra; 1D CNN classification accuracy with augmentation vs jitter/scaling/warping; qualitative independent medical evaluation; delineator validation vs cardiologist annotations (sens/PPV/F1/MAE) and vs ecgpuwave, NeuroKit2, Hamilton-Tompkins; ablations
notes: MIT-BIH: MSE 0.042, DTW 2.29, WD 0.120, PQRST acc 94.1%; PTB-XL 0.057/2.47/0.131/92.8%; simulated 0.049/2.52/0.113/93.0% (vs best baseline TSGAN, avg 37% better MSE). Augmentation accuracy 82.5→90.5% (MIT-BIH), 81.7→89.9% (PTB-XL) vs ≤88.2% for warping (abstract says 'up to 7.2%'). SampEn 1.39 vs 1.43 (p=0.18), RR CV 8.3 vs 8.7%. Caveats: MSE/DTW between unconditional samples and real signals with no stated pairing; real signals wavelet-denoised but synthetic not; most table values only in images; 'medical evaluation' is unquantified.

title: Uncertainty-Aware PPG-2-ECG for Enhanced Cardiovascular Diagnosis using Diffusion Models
authors: Omer Belhasin; Idan Kligvasser; George Leifman; Regev Cohen; Erin Rainaldi; Li-Fang Cheng; Nishant Verma; Paul Varghese; Ehud Rivlin; Michael Elad
model_family: Diffusion (conditional DDPM-style denoiser for PPG->ECG; reverse ECG->PPG model for data completion); UA-P2E uncertainty-aware classification
datasets: MIMIC-III matched waveform (PPG-ECG pairs); PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (11 lead-II-detectable conditions, with synthesized PPG)
loss_functions: diffusion noise-prediction (denoiser epsilon(X_t,Y,t)); classifier cross-entropy
eval_metrics: RMSE (single sample and MMSE/mean of K=100 samples); Frechet Distance (1-FD single sample, 100-FD multi-sample); ROC/AUROC of classification strategies; risk-coverage curves for selective classification; conformal calibration guarantees; MSE and PSNR training curves; pairwise synthetic ECG distances
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (FD as in RDDM/CardioGAN reported metrics)
notes: Key insight: averaging posterior samples approximates MMSE estimator, giving low RMSE but worse perceptual quality; individual samples have higher RMSE (perception-distortion trade-off, Blau & Michaeli). Diagnosis uses expected score over many ECG samples; uncertainty via sample variability; compared to CardioGAN, RDDM.

title: UniECG: Understanding and Generating ECG in One Unified Model
authors: Jiarui Jin; Haoyu Wang; Xiang Lan; Jun Li; Hongyan Li; Shenda Hong
model_family: LLM (unified multimodal LLM with special ECG tokens mapped to frozen DiffuSETS text-conditioned latent diffusion; 'UniECG')
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (737,875 training; 10,000 held-out eval); GEM test set (2,381) for explanation
loss_functions: Weighted NLL for ECG_START/ECG token emission (L_e) + MSE between mapper output and frozen DiffuSETS text embedding (L_d)
eval_metrics: FID; Precision; Recall; F1 (signal-level, precision/recall-based); HR MAE; CLIP score (ECG-text); generation success rate; explanation scored by LLM judge (GLM-5) under ECG-R1 rubric
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: DiffuSETS evaluation protocol embeddings (specific encoder not named in text)
notes: Signal-, feature- and diagnostic-level metric hierarchy. UniECG vs DiffuSETS: FID 79.43 vs 25.26, recall 0.615 vs 0.709 while precision ~equal (0.939 vs 0.941) - shows precision/recall separates fidelity from coverage. 95.61% decoding success rate.

title: Variational autoencoder–based neural electrocardiogram synthesis trained by FEM-based heart simulator
authors: Ryo Nishikimi; Masahiro Nakano; Kunio Kashino; Shingo Tsukada
model_family: VAE (conditional VAE, fully connected encoder/decoder) trained on FEM simulator output (surrogate model)
task: other (parameter-conditioned 12-lead ECG synthesis from 16 cardiac parameters; simulator surrogate)
datasets: UT-Heart FEM multi-physics simulator dataset (2,880 ECG variations)

code_available: promised on GitHub (NTT Communication Science Labs) after acceptance; URL not given
notes: Paired evaluation against simulator ground truth; PSNR ~55-65 dB (very high because simulated noise-free signals). PMAE excludes P wave and outlier positions (>100/150 ms). Notes that appropriate metric depends on purpose (e.g. periodicity-focused for arrhythmia). Synthesis takes seconds on a laptop vs supercomputer hours.

title: Versatile Cardiovascular Signal Generation with a Unified Diffusion Transformer
authors: Zehua Chen; Yuyang Miao; Liyuan Wang; Luyun Fan; Danilo P. Mandic; Jun Zhu
model_family: Diffusion (UniCardio: multi-modal diffusion transformer, noise-prediction, continual learning over modality combinations)
task: PPG2ECG / other-modality2ECG; imputation; denoising (also PPG/ECG->BP translation)
datasets: Cuffless BP dataset (pretraining, 339 h ICU PPG/ECG/BP); PTB-XL (ST change, hypertrophy); MIMIC PERform AF; WESAD (HR); MIMIC (SBP/DBP)
loss_functions: Diffusion noise-prediction (epsilon) MSE loss, with continual-learning phases balancing modality combinations
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; Min-RMSE and Min-MAE (minimum over bounded temporal shifts); KS-test statistic; SNR (supplement); RMSE ratio for ablations; downstream accuracy, sensitivity, specificity for ST change, hypertrophy, AF detection; heart-rate MAE; SBP/DBP MAE; clinician assessment by two cardiologists (third for disagreement); inference time
eval_category_tags: fidelity; distribution; clinical; utility-TSTR; expert; efficiency
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (task-specific downstream detectors; details not extracted)
code_available: https://github.com/thu-ml/UniCardio (to be released; code in supplementary materials)
notes: Min-RMSE/Min-MAE over small time shifts tolerate misalignment that inflates pointwise errors - useful pitfall fix. Generated signals evaluated as substitutes for ground truth in diagnosis/vital-sign estimation, including unseen domains. Sample-entropy filtering of training data. Random 80/10/10 segment split (possible subject leakage on pretraining set).

title: Wearable health monitoring with seismocardiography and generative modeling
authors: Skoric, James
model_family: Other (thesis; generative models for SCG and SCG->multimodal reconstruction)
datasets: unknown (abstract only)
loss_functions: unknown (abstract only)
eval_metrics: median correlation of reconstructed signals (ECG 0.808, NIBP 0.907, ICG 0.833, PPG 0.929); AUROC of OOD pulmonary hypertension detection with synthetic data (0.51 -> 0.86)
