title: ECG waveform generation from radar signals: A deep learning perspective
authors: Farhana Ahmed Chowdhury; Md. Kamal Hosain; Md. Sakib Bin Islam; Md Shafayet Hossain; Promit Basak; Sakib Mahmud; M. Murugappan; Muhammad E. H. Chowdhury
model_family: Deterministic 1D CNN regression (MultiResLinkNet: LinkNet with MultiRes blocks and ResPaths, deep supervision) vs FPN, UNet, LinkNet
datasets: Schellenberger et al. 24 GHz six-port radar + synchronized ECG dataset (30 healthy subjects; Resting, Valsalva, Apnea scenarios)
n_leads: 1 (single TFM ECG channel; lead not specified)
loss_functions: MSE
eval_metrics: MAE; MSE; temporal Pearson correlation; spectral (PSD) correlation; temporal RRMSE; spectral RRMSE; R-peak detection accuracy/precision/recall/F1 ('Two Average' detector); mean RR, SD RR, mean HR, SD HR, RMSSD vs ground truth; qualitative waveform comparison by authors
notes: MultiResLinkNet best temporal/spectral correlation: Resting 66.1/82.4, Valsalva 60.1/77.1, Apnea 55.3 (temporal)/74.7, RVA 61.9/80.0 (x100); MAE ~0.13-0.15 on [0,1]-normalised ECG; R-peak F1 0.955 (rest) to 0.888 (apnea). Correlations of ~0.6 indicate only approximate morphology; RMSSD nearly doubles (12.95 -> 23.87 ms) in predictions, showing beat-timing jitter that MAE hides; 2026 corrigendum removes irrelevant references. Subject-wise 5-fold CV.

title: Uncertainty‐Guided Diffusion Model for High‐Fidelity ECG Synthesis and Classification
authors: Qi Zhang; Hongyan Li
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM U-Net, cosine schedule, 500 steps, conditioning via Dirichlet posterior-network uncertainty guidance with KL and Bayesian loss terms)
task: class-cond (PTB-XL ECG statements) 12-lead synthesis + downstream classification
datasets: PTB-XL
n_leads: 12 (eight leads shown in beat plots, SSSD-style)
loss_functions: 0.6 x epsilon-MSE + 0.3 x Posterior-Network Bayesian loss (expected CE minus Dirichlet entropy) + 0.1 x KL to Dirichlet prior
eval_metrics: KL divergence; marginal distribution difference (MDD); skewness difference (SD); DTW; autocorrelation difference (ACD); Shapley-style per-lead 'sample-level fidelity' valuation (M=1000); single-cardiologist blinded real/synthetic judgement; median beat plots per lead; PR curves (AUPRC); classifier Se/Sp/F1 on real vs synthetic (RF, AdaBoost, Bagging, SVM, LR, Naive Bayes); t-SNE by guidance type; ablation; inference time
notes: KL 0.89 / MDD 31.04 / SD 0.73 vs SSSD 0.93 / 35.95 / 0.85, WaveGAN 1.37 / 39.80 / 2.94; DTW 2.127 vs real-vs-real 2.009 (SSSD 6.363), ACD 0.723 vs 0.718; ablation without uncertainty KL 1.24, DTW 3.98. Real-vs-synthetic classifier F1 within ~0.4-4 points (e.g. RF 86.29 vs 84.33). Expert test is one cardiologist judging four ECGs; the 'sample-level' Shapley valuation is defined but no results reported, and the TSTR/TRTS protocol behind Table 4 is unclear. Usefully reports a real-vs-real reference for DTW/ACD.

title: Diff-TTE: A Novel Diffusion Model for Text-to-Electrocardiogram
authors: Rongjia Wang; Yihai Fang; Jianhong Dou; Xunde Dong
venue: International Conference on Electronic Information Engineering and Computer Technology (EIECT)
model_family: Diffusion (latent DDPM: 1D conv autoencoder with self-attention + S4 state-space residual noise predictor with AdaLN conditioning on Bio_ClinicalBERT text embeddings; REPA-style representation alignment to a pretrained MRTNet ECG classifier)
datasets: PTB-XL (21,799 ECGs, 8:1:1 split; manually standardised English reports)
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 limb leads derived)
loss_functions: latent noise-prediction MSE + frequency-domain (Fourier) loss on denoised latent + representation-alignment loss (negative cosine similarity to MRTNet teacher features)
eval_metrics: FID (CLIP-pretrained InceptionTime features); improved precision; recall; F1 of precision/recall; baselines SSSD-ECG and DSAT-ECG re-conditioned on text; loss-component ablation
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: InceptionTime initialised by CLIP-style ECG-text pre-training (DiffuSETS-style protocol)
notes: FID 0.861 vs SSSD-ECG 1.426 and DSAT-ECG 1.555; precision 100% for every model and recall 98.8-99.8%, so P/R are saturated and non-discriminative; ablation FID 1.591 (base) -> 1.356 (+freq) -> 0.961 (+REPA) -> 0.861. Despite text conditioning, no text-ECG alignment / condition-adherence metric, no clinical or expert evaluation; the REPA teacher (MRTNet) was trained on PTB-XL, so optimising toward its features may favour the embedding-based FID.

title: Biomedically Informed ECG Synthesis: Customizing Cardiac Cycle Phases with Diffusion Model
authors: Yuxin Lin; Jing Ma; Wei Wang; Zhihao Wu; Suyu Dong; Gongning Luo; Kuanquan Wang
venue: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
model_family: Diffusion (DIFF-ECG: DiffWave-style, 36 residual layers, dilated convs replaced by Semantic ECG Batch Normalization (SPADE-like) blocks, 200 steps)
task: segmentation-mask-conditioned synthesis (P/QRS/T wave location masks -> ECG)
datasets: QT Database (PhysioNet; 105 two-channel 15-min Holter records with expert P/QRS/T onset/peak/offset annotations)
loss_functions: standard DDPM epsilon-MSE
eval_metrics: segmentation-based conditional consistency: onset/offset recall and precision (AAMI 150 ms tolerance) of a real-trained U-Net segmenter on generated ECG vs conditioning masks; train-on-synthetic segmenter tested on real ECG (TSTR) recall/precision; real-data reference
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: UNet-like fully convolutional ECG segmentation network (Moskalenko et al.) trained on real QTDB
notes: Real-trained segmenter on generated ECG: onset R/P 91.37/94.04, offset 92.34/95.74 (SSSD-ECG 90.34/89.07, WaveGAN 80.23/92.23; real 98.34/97.12); synthetic-trained segmenter on real ECG: onset 97.03/96.87, offset 97.64/97.28, near the real-trained 98.34/97.12. Only conditional-consistency metrics are reported: no distribution, diversity, morphology or memorisation metrics, and the 150 ms tolerance is loose relative to P/QRS durations.

title: Coarse-to-fine generative augmentation and cross-modal physiological fusion for imbalanced ECG arrhythmia detection
authors: Majid Sepahvand; Maytham N. Meqdad
model_family: GAN (4-stage coarse-to-fine cascade of deformable-conv generators + spectrally normalised discriminators, hinge loss, warm-started first stage) + Phy-SE-ResNet classifier with HRV cross-attention fusion
task: class-cond minority-class beat augmentation for imbalanced arrhythmia classification
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (Normal/AF/AFL/VF); PTB-XL (NORM/MI/STTC/CD/HYP); Chapman-Shaoxing (Normal/AF/AFL/VT); Fetal ECG (simulated, 4 abdominal leads; Normal/Other/Abnormal)
n_leads: native leads per dataset: 2 (MIT-BIH), 12 (PTB-XL, Chapman), 4 (Fetal ECG)
signal_length_s: 0.6 (R-centred beat windows; cascade configured for T=100 samples, inconsistent)
loss_functions: hinge adversarial loss per stage + L1 inter-stage consistency (mu=10) + energy consistency (nu=1) + discriminator agreement L2 (gamma=0.5); classifier CE + 0.2 x MSE rhythm-regularity auxiliary
eval_metrics: downstream Accuracy, macro-P/R/F1, AUPRC; minority-class recall with/without augmentation; augmentation-strategy comparison (none, oversampling, SMOTE, single-stage cGAN); DTW and Pearson per stage on 200 DTW-matched real/synthetic beat pairs; QRS-duration deviation, P-wave presence rate, R-amplitude deviation; nearest-neighbour DTW to train vs held-out test (memorisation check); cross-dataset transfer; 5-seed 95% CI
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (DTW on raw beats; Pan-Tompkins landmarks)
notes: Final stage DTW 4.4 / PCC 0.95 (G0: 17.9 / 0.71); QRS-duration deviation 6.2 ms, P-wave preserved in 94.1%, R-amplitude deviation 3.8%; NN-DTW to train 9.8 vs held-out 10.3 (no memorisation evidence); augmentation raises mean Acc/F1 to 95.7/93.3 vs single-stage cGAN 93.2/90.5 and none 89.4/85.1; PTB-XL HYP recall 43.2 -> 63.3. Caution: the paper itself states the results are 'preliminary ... to illustrate the intended evaluation protocol' with 'full empirical validation on real training runs' left for future work, and there are internal inconsistencies (T=100 vs 150-sample beats), so numbers should not be treated as validated evidence.

title: Physiologically Validated Synthetic ECG Generation via LLM-Guided Constraint Enforcement
authors: Sujit Bhandari; Robin Chataut
venue: Lecture notes in computer science (ICPR 2026 Workshops, LNCS 17110)
model_family: Hybrid (LLM [Claude Sonnet] emits JSON physiological constraint envelopes; rejection sampling over interpolation, per-class MLP WGAN-GP and per-class 1D-CNN WGAN-GP generators)
task: class-cond (per-class AAMI N/S/V/F beat augmentation with physiological-validity filtering)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (inter-patient DS1/DS2 split of de Chazal)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (n_critic=5, lambda_GP=10); no physiology loss (constraints applied post hoc by rejection sampling)
eval_metrics: constraint rejection rate per class/generator; TRTS accuracy; TSTR accuracy; per-class RBF MMD test; per-class DTW distance ratio; TOST equivalence (delta=0.5 sigma, Bonferroni) on 8 morphological features (amplitude, QRS width, R amplitude, RR, P amp, T amp, ST, energy); pairwise cosine similarity (diversity); RMSE to class template; local-morphology audit (baseline drift, total variation, discontinuities, flatlines); shadow-model membership inference; downstream CNN-BiLSTM macro F1 and per-class F1 over 10 seeds with paired t-tests
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (MMD and TOST on handcrafted morphological features / raw beats)
notes: Unconstrained 1D-CNN-GAN beats rejected: N 96.3%, S 15.8%, V 19.1%, F 36.1% (MLP WGAN-GP 94.7/35.8/70.3/97.8%); constrained 1D-CNN-GAN TRTS 95.7%, TSTR 82.1%, DTW ratio 0.88-0.97, MMD fails globally (p<0.001) but p=0.057 without N; TOST equivalence 1/8 (N), 6/8 (S), 5/8 (V), 3/8 (F). No augmentation significantly beats real-only macro F1 0.321 after Bonferroni; constrained keeps V-F1 0.651 vs 0.598 unconstrained. Only 13% of validated beats pass a local-smoothness audit; MIA accuracy 52.4%.

title: Temporal Latent Priors Improve Sequential Generative Modeling of Full-Length 12-Lead ECGs
authors: Marko Miletic; Murat Sariyar
venue: IEEE International Symposium on Computer-Based Medical Systems (CBMS)
model_family: VAE (sequential VAE with time-indexed latents; LSTM/BiLSTM/CNN-LSTM/Transformer encoders, LSTM decoder, i.i.d. vs learned LSTM autoregressive temporal prior; VAE/IWAE/IAF/InfoVAE-MMD objectives; dual reconstruction + classification head)
task: unconditional (representation learning + reconstruction of full-length 12-lead ECGs; prior sampling explored)
datasets: PTB-XL (21,388 records after label filtering; folds 1-8 train, 9 val, 10 test; 5 superclasses)
loss_functions: heteroscedastic Gaussian NLL reconstruction + beta-annealed KL (to i.i.d. or temporal prior) + lambda * multi-label BCE; IWAE bound, IAF flows, InfoVAE-MMD variants
eval_metrics: reconstruction RMSE; PSNR; Pearson correlation (reconstruction vs input); macro-AUROC and accuracy of classification head; latent active fraction; Holm-corrected paired seed-level tests and Kruskal-Wallis tests; visual inspection of unconditional/impulse-train samples
notes: Temporal prior cuts reconstruction RMSE 16-18% (0.0301 -> 0.0247 at Dz=8) and adds 1.5-1.7 dB PSNR; Transformer encoder best (RMSE ~0.0237, PSNR ~16.3 dB, r ~0.988); macro-AUROC ~0.91 unchanged. All fidelity metrics are on reconstructions (paired), not on generated samples; unconditional prior samples were explicitly not realistic (needle-like QRS, missing P/T, inconsistent cross-lead amplitudes) and were only assessed visually.

title: Continuous multi-step ECG and PPG generation through latent disentanglement
authors: Theekshana Dissanayake; Tharindu Fernando; Simon Denman; Sridha Sridharan; Clinton Fookes
model_family: Hybrid (2D-conv autoencoder on magnitude/phase spectrogram with subject code z_p and temporal code z_t; time-shift encoder trained with conditional latent discriminator; reconstruction discriminator; recurrent seed-conditioned rollout)
task: seed- and subject-conditioned multi-step continuation (ECG, PPG); exploratory latent style transfer
datasets: EPHNOGRAM (ECG channel; 17 subjects, 28 good-quality recordings); PhysioNet arterial blood-pressure monitoring dataset (PPG; 7 subjects)
signal_length_s: 2.0 s ECG steps (seed + 2 steps ~6 s reliable, ~8 s for 7/17 subjects); 1.2 s PPG steps (up to 6 forward steps)
loss_functions: MSE reconstruction; subject cross-entropy; cyclic (latent-swap) reconstruction MSE; shift-encoder loss = conditional latent adversarial CE + lambda*(latent MSE + shifted-reconstruction MSE); auxiliary reconstruction-adversarial loss (ECG)
eval_metrics: peak cross-correlation ratio CorrX (lag-maximised, normalised by reference autocorrelation) per forward step vs ground-truth future segment; NeuroKit2 R-peak detection ratio; R-peak temporal deviation; mean RR-interval absolute error; NeuroKit2 PQRST delineation success; subject-ID classifier trained on synthetic tested on real (F1); predicted/actual diastolic BP ratio (PPG); t-SNE of latent codes; qualitative style transfer
code_available: upon request (reference implementation stated as available but URL placeholder '[URL]' in PDF)
notes: ECG CorrX averages 0.81 (reconstruction), 0.58 (t+1), 0.42 (t+2), 0.20 (t+3); 13/17 subjects >=0.30 at t+2; R-peak deviation 0.226 s and RR error 0.270 s (a large fraction of a beat); subject-ID classifier F1 56% real vs 31% synthetic (67% only after excluding poorly generated subjects). PPG CorrX 0.95 -> 0.54 over 6 steps, BP ratio 0.88-1.11. Caveats: within-recording segment-level 90/10 split with possible overlapping windows (leakage), no baseline model, ad-hoc 0.30 threshold, metric can exceed 1.

title: SpectroMamba Flow Matching (SMFM): Fast ECG Generation via 2D Dual-Channel Spectrograms
authors: Peng Zhao; Si Shi; Fei Richard Yu; Zhixing Yuan; Bing Dai
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
model_family: FlowMatching + SSM (class-conditional flow matching on 33x33 real/imaginary STFT spectrograms, 6-layer bidirectional Mamba over 121 patch tokens, DPM-Solver++ 10 steps, inverse STFT)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (78,798 187-sample beat segments, 5 classes; Kaggle/Kachuee-style preprocessing)
fs_hz: not reported (187-sample beats; Kaggle/Kachuee version is 125 Hz)
signal_length_s: not reported (187 samples, ~1.5 s at 125 Hz)
loss_functions: inverse-frequency class-weighted flow-matching velocity MSE
eval_metrics: DTW similarity; F1-score (overall and per class, classifier protocol unclear); TSTR / real+synthetic macro F1; inference time per batch; GPU memory; sampling steps; ablations (bidirectionality, padding, channels)
notes: DTW 0.176±0.008 and F1 0.751±0.012 vs DDPM-ECG 0.245/0.681, VAE-GAN 0.289/0.645; 0.28 s vs 28.4 s per batch, 3.1 vs 8.2 GB, 10 vs 1000 steps; fusion-class F1 0.340 -> 0.582 with weighting. TSTR macro F1 ~0.80 vs real ~0.92, real+synthetic ~0.93 (reported only approximately). DTW pairing protocol and the classifier behind the headline F1 are unspecified; no distributional, diversity, or clinical metrics.

title: Synthesis of Standard 12-Lead ECG from Single-Lead ECG Using Shifted Diffusion Models
authors: Jingwei Liu; Hongyan Li; Shenda Hong
venue: Lecture notes in computer science (ECML PKDD 2024, LNAI 14949)
model_family: Diffusion (SD-ECG: time-frequency (STFT) shifted diffusion with learned shift network conditioned on lead I + age/sex; bidirectional Transformer denoiser with lead-correlation cross-attention, T=100)
datasets: PTB-XL (train/test 70/30); Tianchi ECG (31,779 12-lead, zero-shot); MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (zero-shot, classification)
loss_functions: simplified shifted-diffusion x0-prediction L2 loss (unweighted), shift network trained jointly
eval_metrics: per-lead MSE (formula written as mean absolute difference); per-lead discrete Fréchet distance (FD score) vs ground truth; ROC-AUC of an MIT-BIH beat classifier (SVEB/VEB/Fusion) with synthesized-lead augmentation; ablation (TF domain, shift network, patient info); diffusion-step sensitivity; qualitative case study
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (FD is curve Fréchet distance on signals)
notes: PTB-XL average MSE 0.0117 and FD 2.587 vs Nef-Net 0.0184 / 5.074 and GAN 0.0170 / 6.701; best on 10 of 11 leads (V3/V4 MSE ties GAN). MIT-BIH ROC-AUC SVEB 0.802, VEB 0.981, Fusion 0.866. Paired metrics vs ground-truth leads are appropriate for reconstruction, but the 'MSE' formula is an absolute error, only one sample is drawn per input (no uncertainty/diversity), and zero-shot Tianchi results are only shown qualitatively/in ablation.

title: Progressive Two-Stage ECG Signal Generation: From Structural Skeletons to High-Fidelity Detail Refinement
authors: Guangqi Chen; Fan Lin; Yuhang Liu; Wenxuan Dai; Siyi Fang; Qiang Li; Peng Zhang
venue: IEEE International Conference on Bioinformatics and Biomedicine (BIBM)
model_family: GAN (two-stage WGAN-GP: G1 noise -> square-wave P/QRS/T skeleton via FC+LSTM+Conv; G2 refines skeleton with attention fusion of features from real ECG; shared discriminator)
task: class-specific augmentation (separate models for AFIB, AT, AF) for imbalanced rhythm classification
datasets: Resting ECG Segmentation Dataset (RDB; 2,399 10-s recordings with wave segmentation, 12,730 2-s segments; SR/AFIB/AT/AF)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP adversarial loss (both stages) + L1 structural consistency loss between G2 output and G1 skeleton with decaying weight
eval_metrics: intra-class distance and inter-class Euclidean distance, MMD and KL divergence in a feature space (AFIB generation); ResNet-18 classification F1 and per-class recall/precision with augmentation; ablation; qualitative waveform comparison
notes: AFIB: intra-class 8.95, inter-class ED 12.815, MMD 0.010, KLD 0.325 (BI-DCGAN 14.219 / 0.009 / 0.399; RPSeqGAN 13.322 / 0.010 / 0.750); augmented ResNet-18 F1 0.672 vs no augmentation 0.585 and best baseline BI-DCGAN 0.632; ablation F1 0.612. The feature extractor is unspecified, MMD differences are in the third decimal with no variance, and G2 is conditioned on real ECG at generation time, so samples are transformations of real records (memorisation/privacy not assessed).

title: SynSigGAN: Generative Adversarial Networks for Synthetic Biomedical Signal Generation
authors: Debapriya Hazra; Yung-Cheol Byun
model_family: GAN (SynSigGAN: bidirectional Grid-LSTM generator + CNN discriminator)
task: unconditional / class-wise (per-annotation segments) synthesis of ECG, EEG, EMG, PPG
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (ECG); Siena Scalp EEG; Sleep-EDF (EMG); BIDMC PPG and Respiration
n_leads: not reported (MIT-BIH has MLII + one precordial)
signal_length_s: not reported (beat segments based on median RR)
loss_functions: standard GAN generator/discriminator adversarial losses (DWT-based denoising in preprocessing evaluated with SNR, RMSE, PRD)
eval_metrics: Pearson correlation coefficient (mean); MAE; RMSE; PRD; Fréchet distance (discrete curve distance); classification accuracy of other models on synthetic signals; SNR/RMSE/PRD for preprocessing denoising
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (FD is curve-based on raw signals)
notes: ECG: PCC 0.9991, MAE 0.218, RMSE 0.126, PRD 6.343, FD 0.936; baselines PRD 68-119. Established the PCC/MAE/RMSE/PRD/FD 'paired' metric suite later copied widely; pairing of generated vs original signals is not clearly defined for unconditional generation.

title: DeepFake electrocardiograms using generative adversarial networks are the beginning of the end for privacy issues in medicine
authors: Vajira Lasantha Thambawita; Jonas Lynggaard Isaksen; Steven Alexander Hicks; Jonas Ghouse; Gustav Ahlberg; Allan R Linneberg; Niels Grarup; Christina Ellervik; MORTEN SALLING OLESEN; Torben F. Hansen; Claus Graff; Niels‐Henrik Holstein‐Rathlou
model_family: GAN (WaveGAN* and Pulse2Pulse U-Net generator, WGAN-GP)
datasets: GESUS; Inter99 (Danish population studies; MUSE 12SL 'Normal' ECGs only)
loss_functions: WGAN-GP (gradient penalty), 5 critic updates per generator update
eval_metrics: Fraction of synthetic ECGs classified 'Normal' by commercial GE MUSE 12SL algorithm (model selection across epochs); distributions of MUSE-measured HR, P duration, QT, QRS, PR, STJ/R/T amplitudes vs real; QT-RR correlation preservation; covariance structures
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: commercial ECG interpretation program (GE MUSE 12SL) as measurement/diagnostic oracle
notes: 150,000 DeepFake ECGs released; 81.3% classified Normal. Clinical-parameter distributions matched; truncation of HR at clinical boundaries discussed. Privacy claimed but not quantitatively tested (no memorization/MIA).

title: Synthetic ECG Signal Generation Using Probabilistic Diffusion Models
authors: Edmonmd Adib; Amanda S. Fernandez; Fatemeh Afghah; John Jeffery Prevost
model_family: Diffusion (Improved DDPM on 2D GASF/GADF/MTF image embeddings of beats) vs GAN (WGAN-GP)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (MLII; N class for generation, L class for authenticity test)
loss_functions: Improved DDPM hybrid loss L_hybrid = L_simple + lambda L_vlb (cosine schedule); WGAN-GP (Wasserstein + gradient penalty)
eval_metrics: Average DTW distance; average Frechet distance (quality vs real reference rl-rl); MMD^2 (linear kernel, 7000 vs 7000; real-vs-real reference); authenticity test: ResNet34 N vs L classifier trained on imbalanced set augmented with synthetic beats, reporting accuracy, precision, recall, ROC AUC, average precision, PR-AUC
notes: WGAN-GP beat DDPM on all metrics (DTW 2.12 vs 6.36-6.95; MMD 1.0 vs 35.9-44). Good practice: real-vs-real reference values (DTW 2.09, FD 0.718, MMD 0) as baseline floor. 'Authenticity' here means augmentation utility, not privacy. 2D embedding then de-embedding may hurt diffusion.

title: Diffusion-based conditional ECG generation with structured state space models
authors: Juan Miguel Lopez Alcaraz; Nils Strodthoff
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM with structured state space S4 backbone, 'SSSD-ECG'); baselines WaveGAN*, Pulse2Pulse
datasets: PTB-XL
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; remaining 4 reconstructed from limb-lead relations)
loss_functions: DDPM epsilon-prediction L2 loss (class-conditional)
eval_metrics: Classifier-based measures with XResNet1d50 macro AUROC over 71 labels: Train-synthetic/Test-real (TSTR), Train-real/Test-synthetic (TRTS) via fixed reference classifier, Train-synth/Test-synth internal consistency; qualitative beat-level quantile-band plots; conditional label interpolation; clinical Turing test with a cardiologist (44 ECGs, real vs synthetic + diagnosis)
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: pretrained ECG classifier (XResNet1d50 trained on real PTB-XL) used as reference classifier
code_available: https://github.com/AI4HealthUOL/SSSD-ECG (cited as AI4HealthUOL/SSSD-ECG; synthetic PTB-XL copy also released)
notes: AUROC: real 0.9317; SSSD TSTR 0.8402 vs Pulse2Pulse 0.5968, WaveGAN* 0.5816; TRTS 0.9434. Train-synth/test-synth near 0.98-0.995 for all - uninformative. Abandoned alpha-precision/beta-recall due to unstable one-class embeddings. Turing test: cardiologist misdiagnosed 43%, near-chance real/synthetic discrimination.

title: ME-GAN: Learning Panoptic Electrocardio Representations for Multi-view ECG Synthesis Conditioned on Heart Diseases
authors: Jintai Chen; Kuanlun Liao; Wei, Kun; Haochao Ying; Danny Z. Chen; Jian Wu
model_family: GAN (ME-GAN: two-stage generator with Nef-Net decoder, MixNorm disease conditioning; LSGAN + ACGAN-style major discriminator + view discriminator)
datasets: Tianchi ECG (31,779 records, 500 Hz; LAD, RAD, RBBB); PTB (549 records, 1000 Hz)
loss_functions: LSGAN least-squares adversarial loss (a=1, b=0) + auxiliary disease classification CE/BCE (ACGAN-style) + view-discriminator MSE angle-regression adversarial loss (view-consistency)
eval_metrics: relative FID (rFID = FID(gen, X2)/FID(X1, X2), real-real split as normaliser); 1-NN classifier accuracy (1NNC two-sample test); augmentation PR-AUC with 1D ResNet-34; pairwise distance among views within same case vs real baseline; rFID sensitivity to noise/line-segment/blur perturbations
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: 1D Inception pretrained on ImageNet images reshaped to 12x512 (not an ECG model)
notes: Proposes rFID to normalise image-pretrained-feature FID by a real-vs-real FID; validated monotone response to noise, blur, line-segment perturbations; real-real denominator std 0.212 on PTB. Baseline augmentation PR-AUC 0.879. Feature extractor not ECG-trained — a known weakness later addressed by ECG foundation-model FED.

title: Deep Generative Models for Physiological Signals: A Systematic Literature Review
authors: Nour Neifar; Afef Mdhaffar; Achraf Ben Hamadou; Mohamed Jmaïel
model_family: Survey (systematic review of GANs, VAEs, diffusion models for ECG, EEG, PPG, EMG)
datasets: review of 71 studies (55 + 16 expert-added; 2018-2023); most-used datasets include MIT-BIH, PTB/PTB-XL, BIDMC, DEAP, Sleep-EDF
loss_functions: Catalogued: GAN cross-entropy adversarial loss; WGAN / WGAN-GP for stability; LSGAN least-squares loss; SeqGAN policy-gradient (RL) training; VAE reconstruction + KL regularization (trade-off discussed); diffusion denoising objectives
eval_metrics: Augmentation: ED, DTW, PCC, KLD, RMSE, PRD, MAE, FD, KMMD, relative entropy, TWED, Soft-DTW, MMD, multivariate DTW, MSE, EMD, IS, FID, Wasserstein distance, Chamfer distance, JSD, SSIM, cross-correlation, NRMSE; Denoising: SNR, SNRimp, PRD, MSE, RMSE, SSD, MAD, mean correlation, PPE, cosine similarity; Imputation/forecasting: MAPE, RMSE, IS, FID, MAE, CRPS, MSE, CD, EMD, MMD; Modality transfer: MAE, RMSE, PRD, FD, PCC, DTW, HR MAE, Hellinger distance; utility: precision, recall, F1, accuracy, Cohen's kappa; qualitative visual inspection, cardiologist assessment
notes: >60% of studies rely on visual inspection. Most used metrics: RMSE, MAE, MMD, PRD, DTW, FID. Highlights absence of standardized evaluation protocols and calls for a common protocol; notes lack of reproducible comparisons since code often unavailable.

title: Generative adversarial networks in electrocardiogram synthesis: Recent developments and challenges
authors: Laurenz Berger; Max Haberbusch; Francesco Moscato
model_family: Survey/EvalOnly (PRISMA systematic review of GANs for ECG: basic GAN, AC-GAN, C-GAN, DC-GAN, Sim-GAN, Pro-GAN, mixed)
datasets: 30 publications (2019-2022) from Scopus, PubMed, IEEE Xplore, arXiv; reviewed databases: MIT-BIH-A (n=23 studies), MIT-BIH-NSR, PTB, PTB-XL, Chapman, PhysioNet/CinC 2017, TELE ECG, CPSC2018; non-public GESUS, Inter99, CCDD, CSE
signal_length_s: various (0.35 s beats to 10-60 s; most single beats 0.6-1 s)
loss_functions: reviewed: standard minimax GAN, Wasserstein, least squares, BCE, DTW-augmented and loss-sensitive GAN losses
eval_metrics: Catalogues 20 quality metrics in 3 groups: distance (Euclidean, RMSE, PRD, MAE, MSE, curve Fréchet distance, FID, KID, KL divergence, MMD, DTW, MDTW, soft-DTW, TWED), correlation (normalised cross-correlation, Pearson, amplitude difference coefficient), other (GAN-train/GAN-test, cosine similarity); plus visual inspection/loss curves, expert labelling, commercial-algorithm (MUSE 12SL) classification; and classification gains (accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, precision, F1, AUROC) from augmentation
notes: Of 30 studies, 9 quantified signal quality only, 11 classification only, 10 both; 20 distinct quality metrics, no consensus; augmentation raised accuracy/sensitivity by ~6-7% in four studies. Authors argue point-wise distance/correlation metrics (PC near 1 everywhere) reward copying and penalise phase shifts, so they are unsuitable for augmentation-oriented generation; recommend physiological checks (e.g. RR-interval distributions), reporting of confusion matrices and amount of augmented data, and a gold-standard metric set; most work is limited to single beats.

title: ECG ODE-GAN: Learning Ordinary Differential Equations of ECG Dynamics via Generative Adversarial Learning
authors: Tomer Golany; Daniel Freedman; Kira Radinsky
venue: Proceedings of the AAAI Conference on Artificial Intelligence
model_family: GAN (ODE-GAN: generator learns ECG dynamics dh/dt solved with Euler ODE steps; physics-informed with McSharry simulator parameters)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (AAMI inter-patient partition; N, S, V, F)
loss_functions: standard cross-entropy adversarial losses (generator and discriminator); baselines DCGAN cross-entropy, WGAN EM distance
eval_metrics: downstream heartbeat classification (1D-ResNet) trained on real + synthetic: per-class precision-recall curves and operating points (Re, Pr) per AAMI standard
code_available: not reported ('will be shared online', no URL)
notes: Evaluation purely by augmentation benefit (TRTR vs augmented), following SimGAN practice; no direct fidelity or distribution metric. e.g., SVEB (Re 0.40, Pr 0.83) vs SimGAN Pr 0.70. Patient-wise AAMI split.

title: Multivariate Generative Adversarial Networks and Their Loss Functions for Synthesis of Multichannel ECGs
authors: Eoin Brophy; Maarten De Vos; Geraldine B. Boylan; Tomas Emmanuel Ward
model_family: GAN (MVGAN: 2-layer LSTM generator, 2-D CNN discriminator with minibatch discrimination; DP variant)
datasets: MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm; MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
loss_functions: Compared losses: LSGAN; LSGAN-DTW (LSGAN with multivariate DTW penalty term); DTWGAN (MVDTW as criterion); Loss-Sensitive GAN (LS-GAN); LS-GAN-DTW; DP via gradient noise (GAN-DP)
eval_metrics: MMD; multivariate dependent DTW (MVDTW); real-vs-synthetic discriminability by SVC and LSTM classifiers (accuracy near 0.5 = good); membership inference attack (presence disclosure precision/recall vs threshold ε); benchmarks vs multivariate VAE and LSTM
notes: LSGAN-DTW best (4.9% over LSGAN on normalised MMD+DTW). MIA: ~0% recall for ε ≤0.4·mean distance; DP version 0% up to 0.5. Early use of classifier two-sample test and MIA for ECG GANs.

title: Text-to-ECG: 12-Lead Electrocardiogram Synthesis Conditioned on Clinical Text Reports
authors: Hyunseung Chung; Jiho Kim; Joon‐myoung Kwon; Ki‐Hyun Jeon; Min Sung Lee; Edward Choi
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
model_family: AR-Transformer (Auto-TTE: VQ-VAE tokenizer + autoregressive Transformer decoder + HiFi-GAN decoder); baselines DDPM-style diffusion on raw 12-lead, Tacotron 2 + Griffin-Lim / HiFi-GAN
task: text-cond (clinical text reports + age/sex patient-specific embedding)
datasets: PTB-XL (21,833 text-ECG pairs); private Sejong General Hospital dataset (37,329 pairs)
loss_functions: VQ-VAE: L2 reconstruction + codebook + commitment (stop-gradient) losses; Transformer: token cross-entropy; HiFi-GAN: LS-GAN adversarial (MSD+MPD) + L1 STFT spectrogram loss + L1 discriminator feature-matching loss (weights 1, 2, 45)
eval_metrics: AUROC of ResNet-34 multi-label classifier on samples generated from diagnosis prompts (6 classes); CLIP score (ECG-text contrastive encoder); FID using self-supervised ECG model pretrained on PhysioNet 2021 (64-d features); precision and recall (Kynkaanniemi et al.); cardiologist ranking (3 cardiologists, text-ECG alignment and realism, 100 samples); 10x bootstrap mean/std and t-tests
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: self-supervised ECG model pretrained on PhysioNet/CinC 2021 (last layer modified to 64-d)
notes: Auto-TTE FID 7.17, precision 0.946, recall 0.842; avg AUROC 0.857; CLIP score 0.644. Early text-conditioned ECG work introducing CLIP-style text-ECG alignment score and ECG-FID with SSL encoder; bootstrap + significance testing.

title: CardioGAN: An Attention-based Generative Adversarial Network for Generation of Electrocardiograms
authors: Subhrajyoti Dasgupta; Sudip Kumar Das; Ujjwal Bhattacharya
venue: International Conference on Pattern Recognition (ICPR 2020, held Jan 2021)
model_family: GAN (WGAN-GP; generator = 2 BiLSTM pre-attention layers + Bahdanau-style attention + LSTM post-attention decoder; 1D-CNN critic)
task: unconditional (multi-beat single-lead ECG windows; trained separately per database)
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia; MIT-BIH Normal Sinus Rhythm
fs_hz: 180 (MIT-BIH Arrhythmia 360 Hz subsampled by 2; NSRDB 128 Hz likewise subsampled)
signal_length_s: ~2.8 (512-sample windows at 180 Hz; longer for NSRDB)
loss_functions: Wasserstein loss with gradient penalty (λ=10); ablation vs minimax loss
eval_metrics: PRD; RMSE; discrete Fréchet distance; DTW; visual inspection vs ECGSYN, BiLSTM-GAN, RNN/LSTM-AE, RNN/LSTM-VAE; RR-interval regularity and QT interval range (0.36-0.44 s) check; distance-based anonymity check on random real/generated samples; unspecified 'clinical verification'
notes: CardioGAN PRD 38.6, RMSE 0.157, FD 0.606, DTW 4.15 vs BiLSTM-GAN 66.4/0.276/0.756/9.38 and ECGSYN 78.3/0.363/0.784/15.7; 1D-CNN critic and Wasserstein loss best in ablations. Pairing of real and generated signals for PRD/RMSE is unspecified for an unconditional model; the anonymity and clinical checks are qualitative with no numbers. Not Sarkar's PPG→ECG CardioGAN.

title: Disentangling temporal and amplitude variations in ECG synthesis using anchored GANs
authors: Nour Neifar; Afef Mdhaffar; Achraf Ben-Hamadou; Mohamed Jmaïel; Bernd Freisleben
model_family: GAN (anchored GAN: per-class K-means anchor beats; conv+LSTM generator with amplitude head s and sparse temporal-warping matrix head W, X = W(A + s); conv+LSTM discriminator)
task: class-cond beat synthesis (N, V, F via anchor embedding) for augmentation
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia
n_leads: not reported (single-channel heartbeats from MIT-BIH two-lead records)
signal_length_s: 0.75 (270-sample beats: 350 ms before to 400 ms after R peak)
loss_functions: standard GAN adversarial (BCE) + sparsity loss (l1 − l2) on warping matrix
eval_metrics: qualitative visual comparison of real vs synthetic beats and warping matrices; per-class precision, recall, F1 of three beat classifiers (Kachuee ResNet, Acharya CNN, Kumar MLP) trained on real, real+standard-GAN, real+anchored-GAN beats and tested on real
notes: Augmentation mainly helps minority fusion class: F-class F1 0.81→0.85 (standard GAN)→0.90 (anchored) for classifier 1, 0.85→0.88→0.89 and 0.85→0.89→0.91 for the others; N and V already ~0.99-1.0. No fidelity, distribution or diversity metrics; authors note generated beats contain more artefacts than real; synthetic sample counts and train/test split not reported.

title: BioDiffusion: A Versatile Diffusion Model for Biomedical Signal Synthesis
authors: Xiaomin Li; Mykhailo Sakevych; Gentry Atkinson; Vangelis Metsis
model_family: Diffusion (U-Net DDPM, unconditional / label-conditional / signal-conditional; 'BioDiffusion')
task: unconditional; class-cond; augmentation; also denoising, imputation, super-resolution
datasets: MIT-BIH Arrhythmia (5-class beat version at 125 Hz); UniMiB SHAR (accelerometer); simulated shapes dataset
loss_functions: Diffusion denoising loss with L1 norm (cosine noise schedule, 1000 steps)
eval_metrics: Wavelet coherence; Discriminative score (2-layer LSTM real-vs-synthetic classifier error, TimeGAN-style); UMAP projections; visual inspection; downstream 1D-CNN per-class F1 / precision / recall on MIT-BIH with synthetic augmentation
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (discriminative score uses a trained post-hoc LSTM classifier)
code_available: source code link stated in paper (URL not recoverable from extracted text)
notes: Compared with C-RNN-GAN, RCWGAN, TimeGAN, SigCWGAN, TTS-GAN, TTS-CGAN. Wavelet coherence (0-1) between real and synthetic is unusual for ECG and captures time-varying spectral agreement. Diffusion loss uses L1 rather than L2.

title: Personalized Heart Disease Detection via ECG Digital Twin Generation
authors: Yaojun Hu; Jintai Chen; Lianting Hu; Dantong Li; Jiahuan Yan; Haochao Ying; Huiying Liang; Jian Hui Wu
model_family: Hybrid (GAN + VQ: LAVQ-Editor with VQ-Separator / Disease Embedding Codebook, ClinicalBERT text guidance, AdaIN decoder, StyleGAN-like discriminator)
task: text-cond / other (ECG editing: personalised 'digital twin' disease ECGs from a healthy patient ECG + reference disease ECG/report)
datasets: PTB-XL (single-label superclasses; 291 test patients with both normal and disease ECGs)
fs_hz: not reported (segments R1-100 to R7+100 samples rescaled to 4096 points)
loss_functions: Generator: non-saturating logistic adversarial loss + L2 reconstruction + cosine disease-similarity loss + VQ loss; Discriminator: logistic adversarial loss + cosine disease-feature similarity loss
eval_metrics: Fréchet ResNet Distance (FRD); ResNet Score (RS, Inception-Score analogue); k-NN precision, recall (Kynkäänniemi) and their F1; membership inference risk (F1 of distance-threshold attack in ResNet feature space, ε = τ·mean distance); patient-level personalised accuracy/F1 and Average Treatment Effect (ATE); ECG-level accuracy, F1, AUROC of 1D ResNet-34/GoogleNet; DTW to patient's real ECG (ablation); t-SNE of personal-information retention
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: 1D ResNet-101 pretrained on PTB-XL training set (FRD, RS, precision/recall, MIA distances)
notes: FRD real 0.30 vs ours 1.63 vs baselines 3.8-5.4; CGAN precision 0.997 but recall 0.069 — illustrates why precision alone misleads (mode collapse). MIA evaluated across thresholds τ. Compared CGAN, WGAN, StyleGAN, VQ-VAE2, PGANs.

title: A Comprehensive Evaluation Framework for Synthetic ECG: Assessing Fidelity, Utility, and Privacy
authors: Yixin Li
model_family: Diffusion (SSSD-ECG: conditional DDPM with bidirectional S4 residual layers, 36 layers, 256 channels, 200 steps)
task: evaluation (framework benchmarking label-conditional 12-lead ECG generation by SSSD-ECG on PTB-XL)
datasets: PTB-XL (100 Hz; folds 1-8 train, 9 validation, 10 test)
n_leads: 12 (8 independent leads I, II, V1-V6 generated; III, aVR, aVL, aVF derived)
loss_functions: MSE between true and predicted noise (standard DDPM noise-prediction loss)
eval_metrics: TSTR/TRTR AUROC, F1, sensitivity, specificity (1D-ResNet, bootstrap CIs); LSTM one-step forecasting RMSE, MAE, Pearson r; ACF MAE; Welch PSD log-MAE; FastDTW nearest-neighbour RS/RR distances and DTW ratio; DWT (db4) energy MAE; NeuroKit2 clinical feature MAPE (HR, RR, SDNN, RMSSD, QRS count, R-wave amplitude); DCR and NNDR ratios; 7 MIAs (Euclidean/DTW/wavelet distance, 102-d/47-d/149-d Random Forest classifiers, grey-box denoising-loss) with AUC, TPR@1%FPR, TPR@10%FPR; per-class stratification
eval_category_tags: fidelity; distribution; utility-TSTR; clinical; privacy; conditional; robustness
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: None (no embedding-based metrics; handcrafted features: NeuroKit2 clinical features, 540-d DWT statistics, 102-d relative signal features)
notes: TSTR AUC 0.828 vs TRTR 0.886 (ratio 0.935; HYP lowest at 0.758); forecasting Pearson r 0.918 vs 0.923; ACF MAE 0.0065, PSD log-MAE 0.269, DTW ratio 1.003 (I)/0.994 (V4), but SDNN/RMSSD MAPE ~107-109% (synthetic HRV systematically too high). All MIAs near chance overall (max AUC 0.539 for DTW MIA; per-class max 0.607 for HYP with n_test=56); single model/dataset, single-label subsets only, and clinical features stated as Lead II in methods but Lead I in result tables.

title: P2Es: Physiology-conditioned diffusion for 12-lead ECG generation from PPG
authors: Hui Ji; Wei Gao; Pengfei Zhou
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM-style P2Es with frequency-blur + QRS-adaptive temporal noise forward process, multi-scale conv/attention reverse process, frequency deblurring, 50-step DDIM sampling; KNN + contrastive GroupFinder affinity-matrix conditioning)
datasets: MIMIC-II (GroupFinder clustering); MIMIC-III (benchmarking, cross-dataset); MIMIC-IV (benchmarking, clinical validation, cross-dataset)
loss_functions: Total = 1.0*L_L (inter-lead difference L2) + 0.5*L_F (Fourier/frequency-domain L2) + 0.2*L_Stheta (electrical-axis L2) + 0.3*L_a (signal alignment: R-peak position error + peak-to-peak amplitude range + heart-rate/R-peak-count difference); GroupFinder trained with InfoNCE-style contrastive loss (temperature tau)
eval_metrics: MSE; DTW; Var (variance of generated-minus-GT residual); KL divergence of ECG feature distributions (ST-segment, QRS amplitude); Marginal Wasserstein (MW); electrical axis similarity S_theta; visual comparison; MI/arrhythmia diagnosis sensitivity/specificity/accuracy/precision with confusion matrices; ablation; cross-dataset MSE (MIMIC-III<->IV); params/memory/latency on MacBook and iPhone
notes: On MIMIC-IV P2Es gets MSE 0.0902, DTW 0.0583, KL 0.4920, MW 8.0902, S_theta 0.9542 vs best PPG-to-single-lead baseline PPGG (MSE 0.1078, DTW 0.0792); a Lead-I-to-12-lead DiffWave upper bound has lower MSE (0.0814). Diagnosis on generated ECG: MI specificity 87.5% / sensitivity 68%, SVT/VT accuracy 85%/75%, precision 89%/78%, on small ICD-10 case sets (8-30 per class) with an unspecified classifier; latency 620 ms (M2 Pro) and 4.46 s (iPhone 15 Pro Max), 57M+ params. Caveat: the extracted text is arXiv v1, whose title differs from the published Smart Health version (P2Es); the diffusion noise-prediction loss is not shown explicitly in the total objective.

title: CoFE: A Framework Generating Counterfactual ECG for Explainable Cardiac AI-Diagnostics
authors: Jong-Hwan Jang; Junho Song; Yong-Yeon Jo
model_family: GAN (StyleGAN2 generator + encoder for latent inversion; counterfactuals by gradient descent in latent space guided by a pretrained ECG classifier/regressor)
datasets: MIMIC-IV-ECG (300,000 12-lead ECGs for the generator; 1,000 random recordings for evaluation; ECG-potassium pairs for the regression model); PhysioNet/CinC Challenge 2017 (AF classifier training)
signal_length_s: 10 (stated for the AI-ECG models that consume the counterfactuals)
loss_functions: Standard GAN minimax adversarial loss (generator/discriminator); encoder L2 reconstruction loss ||x - G(E(x))||^2; counterfactual cross-entropy loss CE(f(G(w)), Y_t) minimised over the latent code; (target models: CE for AF classifier, MSE for potassium regressor)
eval_metrics: Mean P-wave amplitude, RR interval variability, T-wave amplitude, QRS duration of original vs counterfactual ECGs with p-values; qualitative comparison with saliency maps
notes: On 1,000 MIMIC-IV ECGs, AF counterfactuals lowered P-wave amplitude 0.09->0.04 mV and raised RR variability 46.17->85.44 ms; potassium counterfactuals raised T-wave amplitude 0.18->0.58 mV and QRS duration 95.84->121.98 ms (all p<0.05). Evaluation is thin: no realism/fidelity, distribution, diversity, or expert metrics for the generator, the statistical test and feature-extraction method are not named, and the AF model is described as 12-lead though trained on CinC 2017.

title: BeatFlow-ECG: Rectified Flow for ECG Reconstruction from Indirect Wearable Signals
authors: Mohamed Kamel; Sahar Selim; Walaa Medhat; Tamer Nadeem
model_family: Flow matching (conditional rectified flow; conv encoder-decoder with transformer bottleneck, AdaRMSNorm time conditioning; 120-step explicit Euler sampling)
datasets: PPG-DaLiA (15 subjects); WESAD (15 subjects)
loss_functions: Motion-weighted L1 velocity-matching (rectified flow) loss with weight w = 1 + alpha*normalised motion score (alpha=1.0) + 0.10 * L1 STFT magnitude loss (nfft 256) on implied ECG estimate; easy-to-hard motion curriculum; baselines: L1 regression (UNet1D/AttnSeq), L1 noise-prediction (Conditional DDPM-1D), adversarial + cycle-consistency (CardioGAN)
eval_metrics: L1; RMSE; Pearson r; R-peak F1 (100-ms tolerance); absolute HR error (bpm); regional Pearson r in P-wave/QRS/T-wave R-peak-relative windows; motion-stratified L1 (low/medium/high); paired Wilcoxon signed-rank tests; 95% CIs across LOSO folds; per-subject tables; params/NFE/inference time; ablation; qualitative reconstructions and peak alignment
notes: Under LOSO, BeatFlow-ECG reaches Pearson r 0.983/0.986, R-peak F1 0.946/0.955 and HR error 4.89/4.12 bpm on PPG-DaLiA/WESAD, with L1 0.062 vs 0.085 (PPG-DaLiA) and 0.055 vs 0.074 (WESAD) for Conditional DDPM-1D; 120 NFE / 425 ms vs 1000 NFE / 3520 ms for DDPM on an H100. Caveats: healthy cohorts only, single-channel z-scored target, no distribution-level or diagnostic metrics, and overlapping windows can be shared between train and validation within training subjects.

title: Presentation Attacks on the PCA-Based Biometric System Using cGAN-Generated ECGs
authors: Chia-Chun Wang; Jui-Kun Chiu; Chih-Hong Lee; Shun-Chi Wu
venue: Annual International Conference of the IEEE Engineering in Medicine and Biology Society (EMBC)
model_family: GAN (conditional GAN, pix2pix-style: FC + 4 transposed-conv generator, FC + 4 conv discriminator)
task: other (beat + RR-interval conditioned continuous ECG trace synthesis for presentation attacks on ECG biometrics)
datasets: PTB Diagnostic ECG (lead I; 285 usable subjects: 100 registered, 85 intruders)
loss_functions: standard conditional GAN adversarial loss (generator and discriminator updated alternately)
eval_metrics: FPIR_attack and FPIR increase over zero-effort attack (at EER threshold) against a PCA-based biometric identification system; FNIR/FPIR/EER of the biometric baseline; inter-beat correlation within synthetic vs real traces; R-R interval variability (qualitative); visual inspection of Q-wave morphology; sensitivity to number of training subjects and pairs
feature_extractor_for_embedding_metrics: none (PCA-based biometric system used as attack target)
notes: Synthetic traces built from template-reconstructed heartbeats raise FPIR by 5.75 percentage points over the 5.39% EER zero-effort baseline (ns=85, np=180). Inter-beat correlation of synthetic traces 0.934 ± 0.122 vs 0.989 ± 0.016 for real (excess beat-to-beat variability), RR variability lower than real and Q waves shallower; RR intervals are random draws within a normal range, so rhythm realism is not modelled. Relevant as a re-identification/privacy-attack use of synthetic ECGs rather than a quality benchmark.

title: Diffusion-based high dimensional subspace mapping for ECG generation with structured state space models
authors: Baofeng Zhu; Chengbao Peng; Xia Zhang; Jiren Liu
model_family: Diffusion (DDPM, 200 steps; SSSD-ECG-style S4 residual layers + patch cross-transformer (vanilla + inverted) with multi-scale convolution; 71 label-specific high-dimensional embedding subspaces trained with semi-hard triplet loss; 127.9M params)
datasets: PTB-XL (recommended folds: 1-8 train, 9 val, 10 test; synthetic replica of same size and label distribution)
n_leads: 12 (8 generated: I, aVF, V1-V6; 4 limb leads derived)
loss_functions: DDPM noise-prediction loss + semi-hard triplet loss over 71 label subspaces (equal weights)
eval_metrics: macro-AUROC (71 labels) of XResNet1d50 under TRTR / TSTR / TRTS / TSTS; ablation via same AUROC grid; qualitative 12-lead comparisons vs SSSD-ECG for NORM, IRBBB, PVC/PAC, sinus tachycardia, atrial flutter; unblinded review by three cardiologists; parameter count
notes: TSTR macro-AUROC 0.8612 vs SSSD-ECG 0.8402, Pulse2Pulse 0.5968, WaveGAN* 0.5816 (TRTR 0.9317); TRTS 0.9576 vs SSSD 0.9434, i.e. higher than real-on-real, suggesting prototypical/low-diversity samples rather than superior realism; TSTS 0.9967. No signal-level fidelity, distribution or diversity metric, no privacy test despite privacy motivation; cardiologist review is unblinded, unscored and compared only to SSSD-ECG on hand-picked examples; ~40 s per sample generation.

title: Radar2ECG: Multi-Scale Bottleneck Fusion and Cross-modal Semantic Distillation for Conditional Electrocardiogram Generation from Radar Heart Sound
authors: Jinye Li; Aidong Men; Yang Liu; Pengda Han; Qingchao Chen
venue: IEEE International Conference on Acoustics Speech and Signal Processing
model_family: Autoencoder-based deterministic translation (1D ResNet-50 encoder (3 stages) + multi-scale fusion bottleneck + 1D DeResNet-50 decoder; pre-trained heart-sound and ECG autoencoders; teacher-student feature distillation from ECG decoder); not a stochastic generative model
task: radar heart sound -> ECG translation (plus anomaly detection on synthetic abnormal radar signals)
datasets: Schellenberger et al. Scidata radar vital-signs dataset (30 healthy subjects, resting condition, 19,048.6 s; 29,680 train / 7,420 test windows); three synthetic abnormal variants (zeroed segments, added noise, mixed signals)
loss_functions: multi-layer cosine feature-distillation loss + MSE generation loss (weighted sum); autoencoder reconstruction pre-training
eval_metrics: RMSE; MAE; cosine similarity; R2 score (paired generated vs synchronized real ECG); anomaly-detection accuracy on synthetic abnormal datasets; layer-fusion ablation; qualitative waveform plots
notes: RMSE 0.0237, MAE 0.0134, cosine 0.987, R2 0.879 vs best baselines (LSTM RMSE 0.153, U-Net cosine 0.831; SSSD R2 -2.08, CWGAN cosine -0.02); anomaly-detection avg accuracy 99.0%. Caveats: heavily overlapping sliding windows (step 1/4 of width) split 8:2 without stated subject-level separation, so test windows likely overlap training data; all baselines have negative R2, suggesting they were poorly adapted; abnormal data are artificial manipulations; no clinical/interval or distribution metrics.

title: Structure-preserving adversarial multi-segment framework for bidirectional ECG–SCG signal translation
authors: Shahbaz Nazami; Udit Satija; Jimson Mathew
model_family: GAN (CycleGAN with residual self-attention conv encoder-decoder generators, three multi-segment vectored-output LSGAN discriminators per direction covering 0.2/0.6/0.2 s)
datasets: CEBS (combined measurement of ECG, breathing and seismocardiogram; 20 healthy subjects; basal, music, post-music states)
n_leads: 1 (one CEBS ECG channel; lead not specified)
loss_functions: least-squares adversarial loss on vectored discriminator outputs + paired MSE to target (GOL) + cycle-consistency MSE + identity MSE (lambda 25/4/0.04/0.04)
eval_metrics: RMSE; PRD; MAE; Pearson correlation coefficient (per subject, per state, 4 train/test cases); module ablation; window/segment-length ablation; qualitative waveform comparison; training loss curves
notes: SCG→ECG (Case 1, basal): RMSE 0.177, PRD 2.06, MAE 0.116, PCC 0.978 vs prior attentive CycleGAN [Satija 2022] 0.434/4.51/0.303/0.89; ECG→SCG PCC 0.81-0.89 with some subjects collapsing (PCC 0.16-0.39). Segments from each subject are randomly split 75/25 (within-subject, adjacent 1 s windows in train and test), so results are subject-dependent and temporally leaky; only paired point-wise metrics, no clinical (interval/HR) or distributional checks.
